translations.literal: Du Fan, Yang Jian
translations.idiomatic: Du Fan and Yang Jian

translations.idiomatic: (with Qian Shi appended)

translations.literal: Zhang Fu, Lu Wu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu and Lu Wu

sentences.zh: （子沆）〉

translations.literal: (son Hong appended)
translations.idiomatic: (with son Hong appended)

sentences.zh: 杜範，字成之，黃岩人。

translations.literal: Du Fan, styled Chengzhi, was a man of Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fan, whose courtesy name was Chengzhi, came from Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 少從其從祖熚、知仁遊，從祖受學朱熹，至範益著。

translations.literal: In youth he associated with his father's cousins Bi and Zhiren; his father's cousins had received instruction from Zhu Xi, and in Fan this became especially prominent.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he kept company with his father's cousins Bi and Zhiren, who had studied under Zhu Xi; in Fan that learning became especially distinguished.

sentences.zh: 嘉字定元年舉進士，調金壇尉，再調婺州司法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Jintan, and was later transferred to serve as judicial officer in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination, was posted as magistrate of Jintan, and was later reassigned as judicial officer in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹定三年，主管戶部架閣文字。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoding he was put in charge of archival documents in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shaoding he was placed in charge of archival documents in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷大理司直。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the post of Dali Sizhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to the post of investigator in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，改授軍器監丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping he was reassigned as Deputy Director of the Directorate of Arms Production.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duanping he was reassigned as deputy director of the Directorate of Arms Production.

sentences.zh: 明年，入對，言：“陛下親覽大政，兩年於茲。

translations.literal: The following year he had an audience and said: "Your Majesty has personally reviewed great affairs of government; two years have now passed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he had an audience with the emperor and said, "Your Majesty has personally attended to the great affairs of state, and two years have now passed.

sentences.zh: 今不惟未睹更新之效，而或者乃有浸不如舊之憂。

translations.literal: Now not only have we failed to see the effects of renewal, but some even harbor the worry that things are gradually becoming worse than before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet not only have we failed to see the fruits of renewal—some even worry that things are gradually growing worse than before.

sentences.zh: 夫致弊必有原，救弊必有本，積三四十年之蠹習，浸漬薰染，日深日腐，有不可勝救者，其原不過私之一字耳。

translations.literal: Now, that which brings corruption must have a source, and that which remedies corruption must have a root. Vicious practices accumulated over three or four decades, steeped and dyed day after day until they grew deeper and more rotten—some beyond all remedy—have no source other than the single word "private."
translations.idiomatic: Corruption must have a source, and remedy must have a root. Vicious habits piled up over three or four decades, steeped and stained until they rotted deeper by the day—some beyond saving—spring from nothing but the one word "self-interest."

sentences.zh: 陛下固宜懲其弊原，使私意淨盡。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should indeed punish the source of these evils and cause private motives to be utterly purged.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should punish the source of these evils and purge private motives altogether.

sentences.zh: 顧以天位之重而或藏其私憾，天命有德而或濫於私予，天討有罪而或製於私情，左右近習之言或溺於私聽，土木無益之工或侈於私費，隆禮貌以尊賢而用之未盡，溫辭色以納諫而行之惟艱，此陛下之私有未去也。

translations.literal: Yet despite the weight of the heavenly throne, private resentments are sometimes harbored; though Heaven appoints the virtuous, rewards are sometimes lavished through private favor; though Heaven punishes the guilty, judgment is sometimes constrained by private feeling; words from attendants and close associates are sometimes drowned in private listening; useless earth-and-wood works are sometimes extravagantly funded from private expenditure; courtesy is raised to honor the worthy yet they are not fully employed; gentle words are used to receive remonstrance yet it is carried out only with difficulty—this is where Your Majesty's private interests have not yet been removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet despite the weight of the throne, private resentments are sometimes nursed; though Heaven appoints the virtuous, rewards are sometimes handed out through private favor; though Heaven punishes the guilty, judgment is sometimes bent by private feeling; the words of attendants and close associates are sometimes drowned in partial listening; useless building projects are sometimes paid for with lavish private spending; ceremony is raised to honor the worthy yet they are not fully used; gentle words are offered to receive remonstrance yet it is put into practice only with difficulty—this is where Your Majesty's private interests remain.

sentences.zh: 和衷之美不著，同列之意不孚，紙尾押敕，事不預知，同堂決事，莫相可否，集義盈庭而施行決於私見，諸賢在列而密計定於私門，此大臣之私有末去也。

translations.literal: The beauty of shared purpose is not displayed; mutual trust among colleagues is not secured; at the paper's end the edict is countersigned, yet affairs are not known in advance; in the same hall decisions are made, yet none assent or dissent; righteous counsel fills the court yet execution is decided by private opinion; worthy men stand in rank yet secret plans are settled in private houses—this is where the great ministers' private interests have not yet been removed.
translations.idiomatic: The harmony of shared purpose is nowhere seen; colleagues no longer trust one another; edicts are countersigned at the bottom of the page, yet affairs are not known in advance; decisions are made in the same hall, yet no one assents or dissents; righteous counsel fills the court, yet execution is decided by private opinion; worthy men stand in rank, yet secret plans are settled behind private doors—this is where the great ministers' private interests remain.

sentences.zh: 君相之私容有未去，則教條之頒徒為虛文。

translations.literal: If private interests of ruler and minister perhaps remain unremoved, then the promulgation of regulations is nothing but empty words.
translations.idiomatic: If private interests of ruler and minister still remain, then the issuing of regulations is nothing but empty words.

sentences.zh: 近者召用名儒，發明格物致知、誠意正心之學，有好議論者，乃從而詆訾訕笑之，陛下一惑其言，即有厭棄儒學之意。

translations.literal: Recently eminent Confucians were summoned and employed, and the learning of investigating things to extend knowledge and of making the will sincere and rectifying the mind was expounded; yet those who delight in controversy thereupon slandered and mocked it, and once Your Majesty was swayed by their words, there arose the intention to abandon Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Recently eminent Confucians were summoned to office and expounded the learning of investigating things to extend knowledge and of making the will sincere and rectifying the mind; yet those who delight in controversy slandered and mocked them, and once Your Majesty was swayed by their words, you showed an inclination to cast Confucian learning aside.

sentences.zh: 此正賢不肖進退之機，天下安危所係，願以其講明見之施行。

translations.literal: This is precisely the hinge on which the worthy and unworthy advance or withdraw, and on which the safety or peril of the realm depends; I hope that what has been expounded may be seen in practice.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely the hinge on which the worthy and unworthy rise or fall, and on which the safety of the realm depends; I pray that what has been expounded may be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 改秘書郎，尋拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was made Secretariat Gentleman and soon appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a secretariat gentleman and soon appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 奏：“曩者權臣所用台諫，必其私人，約言已堅，而後出命。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In the past the remonstrance and censorial officials employed by powerful ministers were invariably their private men; the wording was settled first, and only afterward was the appointment issued.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "In the past the censorial and remonstrance officials used by powerful ministers were invariably their own men; the wording was fixed first, and only afterward was the appointment issued.

sentences.zh: 其所彈擊，悉承風旨，是以紀綱蕩然，風俗大壞。

translations.literal: Their impeachments all followed the prevailing tone, and for this reason discipline collapsed and custom was greatly corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Their impeachments all followed the prevailing tone, and for this reason discipline collapsed and public morals were deeply corrupted.

sentences.zh: 陛下親政，首用洪谘夔、王遂，痛矯宿弊，斥去奸邪。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty personally took up government, you first employed Hong Zikui and Wang Sui, sharply corrected long-standing abuses, and drove out the wicked and corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty took the reins of government, you first appointed Hong Zikui and Wang Sui, vigorously rooting out entrenched abuses and purging the wicked from court.

sentences.zh: 然廟堂之上，奉制尚多。

translations.literal: Yet in the halls of government, deference to established practice still prevails in many matters.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within the halls of power, deference to old ways still held sway in many matters.

sentences.zh: 言及貴近，或委曲回護，而先行丐祠之請；

translations.literal: When speech touched on the noble and the close, there was sometimes evasive protection, and a request for a temple post was first submitted;
translations.idiomatic: When criticism touched the powerful and the well connected, there was sometimes evasive protection, and a request for a temple sinecure was submitted first;

sentences.zh: 事有掣肘，或彼此調停，而卒收論罪之章。

translations.literal: when affairs met obstruction, there was sometimes mutual accommodation, and in the end the memorial calling for punishment was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: when business met obstruction, parties sometimes compromised—and in the end the memorial calling for punishment was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 亦有彈墨尚新而已頒除目，沙汰未幾而旋得美官。

translations.literal: There were also cases in which impeachment memorials were still fresh yet appointment edicts had already been issued, and after brief dismissal they soon received fine offices again.
translations.idiomatic: There were also cases in which impeachment memorials were still fresh yet appointment edicts had already been issued, and after brief dismissal the accused soon received fine offices again.

sentences.zh: 自是台諫風采，昔之振揚者日以鑠；

translations.literal: From this the spirit of the censorate and remonstrance officials, once bold and uplifting, daily waned;
translations.idiomatic: From that point the bold spirit of the censorate and remonstrance officials, once so vigorous, faded day by day;

sentences.zh: 朝廷紀綱，昔之漸起者日以壞。

translations.literal: and the discipline of the court, once gradually reviving, daily worsened.
translations.idiomatic: and the discipline of the court, once slowly recovering, deteriorated day by day.

sentences.zh: ”理宗深然之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Lizong deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Lizong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 又奏九江守何炳年老不足備風寒，事寢不行。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that He Bing, prefect of Jiujiang, was old and unfit to endure wind and cold; the matter was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that He Bing, prefect of Jiujiang, was too old to endure wind and cold; the matter was shelved and not carried out.

sentences.zh: 範再奏曰：“一守臣之未罷其事小，台諫之言不行其事大。

translations.literal: Fan memorialized again, saying: "That one prefect was not removed is a small matter; that the words of the censorate and remonstrance officials were not heeded is a great matter.
translations.idiomatic: Fan memorialized again, saying, "That one prefect was not removed is a small matter; that the words of the censorate and remonstrance officials were not heeded is a great matter.

sentences.zh: 阻台諫之言猶可也，至於陛下之旨匿而不行，此豈勵精親政之時所宜有哉！

translations.literal: Blocking the words of the censorate and remonstrance officials might still be tolerated, but that Your Majesty's own directive was concealed and not carried out—how can this be fitting in a time when you are striving to govern with vigor and attend personally to affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Blocking the censorate might be tolerated—but that Your Majesty's own directive was buried and never carried out: how can that be fitting in an era when you strive to govern with vigor and attend to affairs in person!

sentences.zh: ”丞相鄭清之見之大怒，五上章丐去，有“危機將發，朋比禍作”之語；

translations.literal: " Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi, on reading this, was greatly enraged and five times submitted memorials requesting dismissal, with words such as "a crisis is about to break out, and the calamity of factional collusion will follow";
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi, reading this, flew into a rage and five times memorialized asking to be dismissed, warning of "a crisis about to break and the calamity of factional collusion";

sentences.zh: 且謂範順承風旨，粉飾擠陷。

translations.literal: he also said that Fan was merely following the prevailing tone, embellishing facts and squeezing others out by false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: he also said that Fan was merely following the prevailing tone, embellishing facts and framing others by false accusation.

sentences.zh: 範遂自劾，言：“宰相之與台諫，官有尊卑而事關一體，但當同心為國，豈容以私而害公。

translations.literal: Fan thereupon impeached himself, saying: "Between the chief councilor and the censorate and remonstrance officials, rank may be high or low, yet the affair concerns one body; they should only join hearts for the state—how can private interest be allowed to harm the public good?
translations.idiomatic: Fan thereupon impeached himself, saying, "Between the chief councilor and the censorate and remonstrance officials, rank may be high or low, yet the affair concerns one body; they should only join hearts for the state—how can private interest be allowed to harm the public good?

sentences.zh: 行之者宰相，言之者台諫。

translations.literal: The one who executes is the chief councilor; the one who speaks is the censorate and remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor executes; the censorate and remonstrance officials speak.

sentences.zh: 行之者豈盡合於事宜，言之者或未免於攻詆，清明之朝，此特常事。

translations.literal: What the executor does may not wholly accord with what the situation requires; what the speaker says may not wholly escape attack and slander—in a clear and enlightened court, this is merely the ordinary course of things.
translations.idiomatic: Those who act may not always match what circumstances require; those who speak may not escape attack and slander—in a clear and enlightened court, this is simply the way of things.

sentences.zh: 古者大臣欲扶持紀綱，故必崇獎台諫，聞有因言而待罪者矣，未聞有諱言而含怒者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity great ministers, wishing to uphold discipline, therefore always honored and rewarded the censorate and remonstrance officials; one has heard of men who awaited punishment because of their words, but one has never heard of men who concealed anger because speech was taboo.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity great ministers, wishing to uphold discipline, therefore always honored and rewarded the censorate and remonstrance officials; one has heard of men who awaited punishment because of their words, but one has never heard of men who nursed anger because speech was taboo.

sentences.zh: 曩者柄臣所用台諫，必其私人；

translations.literal: In the past the censorate and remonstrance officials used by the power-holder were invariably his private men;
translations.idiomatic: In former days the power-holder's censors and remonstrators were always his own men;

sentences.zh: 陛下更新庶政，而台諫皆出於親擢。

translations.literal: Your Majesty renewed the multitude of policies, and the censorate and remonstrance officials all came from personal selection.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty renewed the multitude of policies, and every censor and remonstrator was personally chosen by you.

sentences.zh: 若廟堂不欲臣言其親故，鉗其口，奪其氣，則與曩者之用私人何以異？

translations.literal: If the halls of government do not wish your servant to speak of their kin and friends, clamp his mouth, and steal his spirit, then how does this differ from the past use of private men?
translations.idiomatic: If the halls of government do not wish your servant to speak of their kin and friends, to clamp his mouth and break his spirit—how is that different from employing private men as in the past?

sentences.zh: 不知所謂‘承順風旨’者何人？

translations.literal: I do not know who is meant by "following the prevailing tone."
translations.idiomatic: Who, I wonder, is meant by "following the prevailing tone"?

sentences.zh: ‘粉飾擠陷’者何事？

translations.literal: What affair is meant by "embellishing facts and squeezing others out by false accusation"?
translations.idiomatic: What affair is meant by "embellishing facts and framing others by false accusation"?

sentences.zh: 乞檢臣前奏，賜之罷黜，以從臣退安田裏之欲。

translations.literal: I beg that my former memorials be examined and that dismissal be granted me, so that I may follow my wish to retire in peace to my fields.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that my earlier memorials be examined and that I be dismissed, so that I may retire in peace to my fields as I wish.

sentences.zh: 時清之妄邀邊功，用師河、洛，兵民死者十數萬，資糧器甲悉委於敵，邊境騷然，中外大困。

translations.literal: At that time Qingzhi recklessly sought frontier merit, deployed troops on the He and Luo fronts, and soldiers and civilians died by the hundreds of thousands; supplies, grain, and armor were all abandoned to the enemy; the borderlands were in turmoil, and court and country were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qingzhi recklessly sought frontier glory, sent troops to the He and Luo fronts, and hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians perished; supplies, grain, and armor were all abandoned to the enemy; the borderlands erupted in turmoil, and court and country alike were brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 範率合台論其事，並言製閫之詐謀罔上。

translations.literal: Fan led the censorate in jointly memorializing on the affair, and also spoke of the military commissioner's deceitful plots to mislead the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Fan led the censorate in a joint memorial on the affair, and also exposed the military commissioner's deceitful plots to mislead the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是凡侍從、近臣之不合時望者，監司、郡守之貪暴害民者，皆以次論斥。

translations.literal: Thereupon all attendant officials and close ministers who did not accord with public expectation, and all supervisory commissioners and prefects who were greedy, violent, and harmful to the people, were in turn impeached and denounced.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon every attendant and close minister who failed to meet public expectation, and every supervisory commissioner and prefect who was greedy, violent, and harmful to the people, was impeached and denounced in turn.

sentences.zh: 清之愈忌之，改太常少卿。

translations.literal: Qingzhi grew all the more resentful of him and had him transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi grew all the more resentful of him and had him transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 轉對言：“今日之病，莫大於賄賂交結之風。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he said: "The disease of today is greatest in the wind of bribery and collusion.
translations.idiomatic: At a rotating audience he said, "The disease of today is greatest in the wind of bribery and collusion.

sentences.zh: 名譽已隆者賈左右之譽以固寵，宦遊未達者惟梯級之求以進身。

translations.literal: Those whose reputations are already lofty purchase praise from those around them to secure favor; those in official service who have not yet risen seek only rung upon rung of advancement to make their way forward.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose reputations are already high buy praise from those around them to hold their favor; those who have not yet risen in office seek only the next rung on the ladder.

sentences.zh: 邊方帥臣，黃金不行於反間，而以探刺朝廷；

translations.literal: Frontier commanders do not use gold for counter-intelligence, but use it to spy on the court;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanders do not spend gold on counter-intelligence—they spend it spying on the court;

sentences.zh: 厚賜不優於士卒，而以交通勢要。

translations.literal: generous rewards are not bestowed on the soldiers, but are used to cultivate ties with the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: generous rewards are not lavished on the rank and file—they are used to cultivate ties with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 以致賞罰顛倒，威令慢褻，罪貶者拒命而不行，棄城者巧計以求免，提援兵者召亂而肆掠，當重任者怙勢而奪攘。

translations.literal: The result is that rewards and punishments are reversed, authority and commands are treated with contempt, those condemned to punishment refuse the order and do not go, those who abandon cities devise schemes to escape blame, those who lead relief troops summon disorder and plunder at will, and those who hold heavy responsibility rely on power to seize and grab.
translations.idiomatic: The result: rewards and punishments stand on their heads, authority and command are treated with contempt, those condemned refuse to go, those who abandon cities scheme to escape blame, those leading relief troops summon disorder and plunder at will, and those bearing heavy responsibility rely on power to seize what they want.

sentences.zh: 下至禁旅，驕悍難製，監軍群聚相剽劫。

translations.literal: Down even to the palace guard, they are arrogant, fierce, and hard to control; supervising officers gather in groups and rob one another.
translations.idiomatic: Even the palace guard had grown arrogant and fierce, hard to control; supervising officers gathered in bands and robbed one another.

sentences.zh: 欲望陛下毋以小恩廢大誼，毋以私情撓公法，嚴製宮掖，不使片言得以入於閫；

translations.literal: I desire that Your Majesty not let small favors destroy great principle, not let private feeling bend public law, strictly control the inner palace, and not allow a single word to enter the women's quarters;
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty not let small favors destroy great principle, not let private feeling bend public law, strictly control the inner palace, and not allow a single word to enter the women's quarters;

sentences.zh: 禁約閹宦，不使讒諂得以售其奸。

translations.literal: restrain and bind the eunuchs, and not allow slander and flattery to sell their wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: restrain the eunuchs, and do not let slander and flattery sell their wickedness.

sentences.zh: ”範自入台，屢丐祠，至是復五上歸田之請，皆不允。

translations.literal: " From the time Fan entered the censorate he repeatedly requested temple posts, and on this occasion again submitted five requests to return to his fields; all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: " From the time Fan entered the censorate he had repeatedly asked for a temple post; now he again submitted five requests to return to his fields—all refused.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Lecturer at the Hall for Explicating Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Secretariat and concurrently lecturer at the Hall for Explicating Governance.

sentences.zh: 大元兵徇江陵，範乞屯兵蘄、黃以防窺江，且令沿江帥臣兼江、淮製置大使以重其權，令淮西帥臣急調兵撥糧以援江陵。

translations.literal: When the Great Yuan army marched on Jiangling, Fan requested that troops be stationed at Qi and Huang to guard against a crossing of the Yangtze, and further that the commanders along the river concurrently serve as commissioners for Jiang-Huai military affairs to increase their authority, and that the Huai-west commander urgently mobilize troops and allocate grain to aid Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Yuan army marched on Jiangling, Fan requested that troops be stationed at Qi and Huang to guard against a crossing of the Yangtze, and further that the commanders along the river concurrently serve as Jiang-Huai military commissioners to increase their authority, and that the Huai-west commander urgently mobilize troops and allocate grain to aid Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 拜殿中侍御史，辭不獲，乃因講筵，奏：“臣嚐冒耳目之寄，輒忤宰相，至煩陛下委曲調護，今又使居向者負芒之地，豈以臣絕私比，而其言猶有可取耶？

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant Censor; unable to decline, he thereupon memorialized at the classics lecture: "Your servant once presumptuously received the charge of being the emperor's eyes and ears, and repeatedly offended the chief councilor, so much so that Your Majesty had to make tactful efforts to protect me; now I am again placed in the position where I once bore thorns—can it be because your servant rejects private faction, and yet his words still have something worth taking?
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed palace attendant censor; unable to decline, he thereupon memorialized at the classics lecture, "Your servant once presumptuously received the charge of being the emperor's eyes and ears, and repeatedly offended the chief councilor, so much so that Your Majesty had to make tactful efforts to protect me; now I am again placed in the position where I once bore thorns—can it be because your servant rejects private faction, and yet his words still have something worth taking?

sentences.zh: 抑以臣巽懦之質，易於調護，而姑使之備數耶？

translations.literal: Or is it because your servant's yielding and timid nature makes him easy to manage, and he is for the moment kept merely to fill a number?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it because your servant's yielding, timid nature makes him easy to manage—and he is kept on merely to fill a seat?

sentences.zh: 昔人主之於諍臣，非樂而聽之，即勉而從之，否則疏而遠之，未聞有不用其言而復用其人者。

translations.literal: In former times, when rulers faced remonstrating ministers, they either gladly listened, or urged themselves to follow, or else kept them at a distance; one never heard of not using a man's words yet employing the man again.
translations.idiomatic: In former times rulers facing remonstrating ministers either listened gladly, urged themselves to follow, or kept them at a distance; one never heard of ignoring a man's words yet employing the man again.

sentences.zh: 陛下自端平親政以來，召用正人以振台綱，未幾而有委曲調護之弊，其所彈擊，或牽製而不行，其所斥逐，復因緣以求進。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty personally took up government in the Duanping era, upright men were summoned and employed to revive the discipline of the censorate; before long there arose the abuse of tactful protection; impeachments were sometimes obstructed and not carried out, and those who were denounced and driven out again sought advancement through connections.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty personally took up government in the Duanping era, upright men were summoned to revive censorate discipline; before long the abuse of tactful protection arose—impeachments were obstructed and not carried out, and those driven out sought advancement again through connections.

sentences.zh: 臣於入台之初，固已力言之，不惟不之革，而其弊滋甚，甚至節貼而文理不全，易寫而台印無有，中書不敢執奏，見者為之致疑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your servant's entry into the censorate, I had already spoken forcefully on this; not only was it not reformed, but the abuse grew worse, even to the point where attached sections were incomplete in composition and logic, copies could easily be made yet the censorate seal was nowhere to be found, the Secretariat dared not submit them, and those who saw this were moved to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: When your servant first entered the censorate, I had already spoken forcefully on this; not only was nothing reformed—the abuse grew worse, until attached sections were incomplete in logic and composition, copies could easily be made yet the censorate seal was nowhere to be found, the Secretariat dared not submit them, and those who saw this were moved to doubt.

sentences.zh: 不意聖明之時，其弊一至於此。

translations.literal: I did not expect that in so sage and enlightened a time the abuse would reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that in so sage and enlightened an age the abuse would reach this point.

sentences.zh: 陛下以其言之不可用，又從而超遷之，則是台諫之官，專為仕途之捷徑。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because his words could not be used, then went on to promote him by special advancement—then the office of censorate and remonstrance becomes nothing but a shortcut on the path of official career.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, because his words could not be used, then promoted him by special advancement—making the censorate nothing but a shortcut on the path of official career.

sentences.zh: 陛下但知崇獎台諫為盛德，而不知阻抑直言之為弊政，則陛下外有好諫之名，內有拒諫之實，天下豈有虛可以蓋實哉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty knows only to honor and reward the censorate and remonstrance officials as a great virtue, but does not know that obstructing straightforward speech is a corrupt policy; then Your Majesty outwardly has the name of welcoming remonstrance, yet inwardly has the reality of rejecting remonstrance—can the empty cover the real under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows only to honor and reward the censorate as a great virtue, but does not know that obstructing straightforward speech is a corrupt policy; outwardly you have the name of welcoming remonstrance, yet inwardly you reject it—can the empty cover the real under Heaven?

sentences.zh: ”範始以不得其言不去為恨，至是遂極言台諫失職之弊。

translations.literal: " Fan had at first resented that he did not leave because his words were not heeded; on this occasion he therefore spoke to the utmost on the abuse of the censorate and remonstrance officials' dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan had at first resented that he did not leave when his words went unheeded; now he spoke to the utmost on the censorate's dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 時襄、蜀俱壞，江陵孤危，兩浙震恐，復言：“清之橫啟邊釁，幾危宗祀，及其子招權納賄，貪冒無厭，盜用朝廷錢帛以易貨外國，且有實狀。

translations.literal: At that time Xiang and Shu were both ruined, Jiangling stood isolated and imperiled, and the two Zhe regions were shaken with fear; he again said: "Qingzhi recklessly opened frontier conflict and nearly endangered the imperial altars; moreover his son gathered power and accepted bribes, was greedy and insatiable, stole and used the court's money and silks to trade goods with foreign states, and there is solid evidence of this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiang and Shu were both ruined, Jiangling stood isolated and imperiled, and the two Zhe regions were shaken with fear; he again said, "Qingzhi recklessly opened frontier conflict and nearly endangered the imperial altars; moreover his son gathered power and accepted bribes, was greedy and insatiable, stole and used the court's money and silks to trade goods with foreign states, and there is solid evidence of this.

sentences.zh: ”並言：“簽書樞密院事李鳴復與史寅午、彭大雅以賄交結，曲為之地。

translations.literal: " He also stated: "Li Mingfu, Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, formed corrupt ties through bribery with Shi Yinwu and Peng Daya, bending the law to shield them.
translations.idiomatic: " He also stated, "Li Mingfu, associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, formed corrupt ties through bribery with Shi Yinwu and Peng Daya, bending the law to shield them.

sentences.zh: 鳴復既不恤父母之邦，亦何有陛下之社稷。

translations.literal: Mingfu does not even care for the land of his parents—how much less does he care for Your Majesty's altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: Mingfu does not even care for the land of his parents—how much less for Your Majesty's altars of state!

sentences.zh: ”帝以清之潛邸舊臣，鳴復未見大罪，未即行，範亦不入台。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because Qingzhi was an old retainer from his princely residence and Mingfu had not been seen to commit a grave crime, did not act at once; Fan also did not enter the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor held back—for Qingzhi was an old retainer from his princely days, and Mingfu had not been shown to have committed a grave crime; Fan, too, did not enter the censorate.

sentences.zh: 帝促之，範奏：“鳴復不去則臣去，安敢入經筵？

translations.literal: The emperor urged him; Fan memorialized: "If Mingfu is not removed, then your servant will leave—how dare I enter the classics lecture?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urged him; Fan memorialized, "If Mingfu is not removed, then your servant will leave—how dare I enter the classics lecture?

sentences.zh: ”方再奏之，鳴復抗疏自辨，言：“台臣論臣，不知所指何事，豈以臣嚐主和議耶？

translations.literal: " Just as he was memorializing again, Mingfu submitted a forceful memorial in self-defense, saying: "The censorial official impeaches your servant, but I do not know to what affair this refers—can it be because your servant once advocated peace talks?
translations.idiomatic: " Just as he was memorializing again, Mingfu submitted a forceful memorial in self-defense, saying, "The censorial official impeaches your servant, but I do not know to what affair this refers—can it be because your servant once advocated peace talks?

sentences.zh: 幸未斥退，則安國家、利社稷，死生以之；

translations.literal: If fortunately I am not dismissed and driven out, then to secure the state and benefit the altars of the realm I will stake my life upon it;
translations.idiomatic: If fortunately I am not dismissed, then to secure the state and benefit the altars of the realm I will stake my life upon it;

sentences.zh: 否則無家可歸，惟有扁舟五湖耳。

translations.literal: otherwise I have no home to which to return, and have only a small boat upon the Five Lakes.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I have no home to return to—only a small boat upon the Five Lakes.

sentences.zh: ”範又極言其寡廉鮮恥，既而合台劾之，太學諸生亦上書交攻之。

translations.literal: " Fan again spoke to the utmost of his lack of integrity and shame, and then jointly with the censorate impeached him; the students of the Imperial Academy also submitted memorials attacking him in turn.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan again spoke to the utmost of his lack of integrity and shame, then jointly with the censorate impeached him; students of the Imperial Academy also submitted memorials attacking him in turn.

sentences.zh: 鳴復將出關，帝又遣使召回，範復與合台奏：“鳴復為宰執，所交惟史寅午、彭大雅，此等相與陰謀，不過賂近習、蒙上聽，以陰圖相位。

translations.literal: Mingfu was about to leave the capital when the emperor again sent envoys to recall him; Fan again jointly memorialized with the censorate: "Mingfu, as a chief minister, associates with none but Shi Yinwu and Peng Daya; such men plot together in secret, doing nothing but bribing close attendants and deceiving what the emperor hears, in order secretly to seek the position of chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Mingfu was about to leave the capital when the emperor again sent envoys to recall him; Fan again jointly memorialized with the censorate, "Mingfu, as a chief minister, associates with none but Shi Yinwu and Peng Daya; such men plot together in secret, doing nothing but bribing close attendants and deceiving what the emperor hears, in order secretly to seek the position of chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 臣近見自辨之章，見其交鬥邊臣以啟嫌隙，妄言和戰以肆脅持，且以蜀既破蕩而欲泛舟五湖，又以安國家、利社稷自任，不知鳴復久居政府，今又有何安利之策？

translations.literal: Your servant recently saw his memorial of self-defense and observed that he incited frontier officials against one another to open rifts of suspicion, spoke recklessly of peace and war to wield coercion, and though Shu has already been ravaged and destroyed yet spoke of drifting in a small boat upon the Five Lakes, while also taking upon himself the charge of securing the state and benefiting the altars of the realm—I do not know what policy Mingfu, long seated in government, now has that could bring peace and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant recently saw his memorial of self-defense: he had incited frontier officials against one another to open rifts of suspicion, spoken recklessly of peace and war to wield coercion, and though Shu has already been ravaged yet spoke of drifting upon the Five Lakes—while also taking upon himself the charge of securing the state and benefiting the altars of the realm. What policy, I ask, does Mingfu—long seated in government—now have that could bring peace and profit?

sentences.zh: 欺君罔上，無所不至。

translations.literal: Deceiving the ruler and misleading the throne—there is nothing to which he will not go.
translations.idiomatic: Deceiving the ruler and misleading the throne—there is nothing to which he will not stoop.

sentences.zh: 如臣等言是，即乞行之；

translations.literal: If what your servants say is correct, then I beg that it be carried out;
translations.idiomatic: If your servants speak truly, then I beg that it be done;

sentences.zh: 所言若非，早賜罷斥。

translations.literal: if what is said is not so, then let dismissal be granted at once.
translations.idiomatic: if it is not so, then let me be dismissed at once.

sentences.zh: ”改起居郎，範奏：“臣論鳴復，未見施行，忽拜左史之命，則是所言不當，姑示優遷。

translations.literal: " He was made Left Recorder; Fan memorialized: "Your servant impeached Mingfu, yet no action was seen; suddenly I received appointment as Left Recorder—this means that what was said was improper, and I am for the moment shown special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Left Recorder; Fan memorialized, "Your servant impeached Mingfu, yet no action was seen; suddenly I received appointment as Left Recorder—this means that what was said was improper, and I am for the moment shown special advancement.

sentences.zh: 臣前者嚐奏台諫但為仕途之捷徑，初無益朝廷之紀綱，躬言之，躬蹈之，臣之罪大矣。

translations.literal: Your servant earlier once memorialized that the censorate and remonstrance offices were nothing but shortcuts on the path of official career and at first brought no benefit to the court's discipline; to speak it in person and then tread it in person—your servant's offense is great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant earlier memorialized that the censorate and remonstrance offices were nothing but shortcuts on the path of official career and brought no benefit to the court's discipline; to speak it in person and then tread it in person—your servant's offense is great indeed.

sentences.zh: ”即渡江而歸。

translations.literal: " He thereupon crossed the river and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon crossed the river and returned home.

sentences.zh: 授江東提點刑獄，尋改浙西提點刑獄，範力辭之，而鳴復亦出守越。

translations.literal: He was appointed Judicial Intendant for Jiangdong, and soon transferred to Judicial Intendant for Zhexi; Fan forcefully declined, and Mingfu also went out to serve as prefect of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial intendant for Jiangdong, and soon transferred to judicial intendant for Zhexi; Fan forcefully declined, and Mingfu also went out to serve as prefect of Yue.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年，差知寧國府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaxi he was assigned to serve as prefect of Ningguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiaxi he was assigned prefect of Ningguo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年至郡，適大旱，範即以便宜發常平粟，又勸寓公富人有積粟者發之，民賴以安。

translations.literal: The following year he reached the prefecture; it happened to be a great drought, and Fan immediately, by expedient authority, released grain from the Ever-Normal Granary, and also urged wealthy retired officials who had stored grain to release it; the people relied on this and were settled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he reached the prefecture in the midst of a great drought; Fan immediately, by expedient authority, released grain from the Ever-Normal Granary and urged wealthy retired officials with stored grain to do the same; the people relied on this and were saved.

sentences.zh: 始至，倉庫多空，未幾，米餘十萬斛，錢亦數萬，悉以代輸下戶糧。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, the storehouses were largely empty; before long there remained more than one hundred thousand hu of rice and several tens of thousands in cash, all of which was used to pay the grain tax on behalf of lower households.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived the storehouses were nearly empty; before long more than one hundred thousand hu of rice and several tens of thousands in cash remained, all used to pay the grain tax on behalf of lower households.

sentences.zh: 兩淮饑民渡江者多剽掠，其首張世顯尤勇悍，擁眾三千餘人至城外。

translations.literal: Many famine refugees from the two Huai regions who crossed the Yangtze engaged in plunder; their leader Zhang Shixian was especially fierce and bold, and led a band of more than three thousand men to the outside of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Many famine refugees from the two Huai regions who crossed the Yangtze turned to plunder; their leader Zhang Shixian was especially fierce and bold, and led more than three thousand men to the foot of the city wall.

sentences.zh: 範遣人犒之，俾勿擾以俟處分，世顯乃陰有窺城之意。

translations.literal: Fan sent men to reward them with provisions and ordered them not to disturb the people while awaiting disposition; Shixian thereupon secretly harbored the intention of spying out the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fan sent men to reward them with provisions and ordered them not to disturb the people while awaiting disposition; Shixian thereupon secretly harbored designs on the city.

sentences.zh: 範以計擒斬之，給其眾使歸。

translations.literal: Fan by stratagem captured and executed him, supplied his followers, and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: Fan laid a trap, captured and executed him, provisioned his followers, and sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 四年，還朝，首言：

translations.literal: In the fourth year he returned to court and first spoke:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to court and spoke first:

sentences.zh: 旱暵薦臻，人無粒食。

translations.literal: Drought and scorching heat came one after another, and people had not a grain to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and scorching heat came one after another, and the people had not a grain to eat.

sentences.zh: 楮券猥輕，物價騰踴。

translations.literal: Paper currency was debased and light, and prices soared upward.
translations.idiomatic: Paper currency had been debased, and prices soared.

sentences.zh: 行都之內，氣象蕭條，左浙近輔，殍死盈道。

translations.literal: Within the traveling capital, the atmosphere was desolate; in Zhejiang to the left, near the imperial auxiliary capital, corpses of the starved dead filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Within the mobile capital the atmosphere was bleak; in neighboring Zhejiang, starved corpses littered the roads.

sentences.zh: 流民充斥，未聞安輯之政，剽掠成風，已開弄兵之萌，是內憂既迫矣。

translations.literal: Displaced people filled everywhere; no policy of settlement and pacification was heard of; plundering became the fashion, and the germ of armed rebellion had already appeared—thus internal worry had already become urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees thronged everywhere, yet no policy of relief and resettlement was heard; plunder became rampant, and the seeds of armed rebellion had already been sown—internal crisis was already pressing.

sentences.zh: 新興北兵，乘勝而善鬥，中原群盜，假名而崛起。

translations.literal: The newly risen northern troops, riding victory and skilled in fighting; bandits throughout the Central Plains, rising under borrowed names.
translations.idiomatic: The newly risen northern armies fought well on the momentum of victory, while bandits throughout the Central Plains rose up under false banners.

sentences.zh: 搗我巴蜀，據我荊襄，擾我淮堧，近又由夔、峽以瞰鼎、澧。

translations.literal: They struck our Ba-Shu, occupied our Jing-Xiang, harassed our Huai frontier, and recently passed through Kuai and the gorges to overlook Ding and Li.
translations.idiomatic: They raided our Ba-Shu region, seized our Jing-Xiang, harassed our Huai frontier, and recently advanced through Kuai and the gorges to threaten Ding and Li.

sentences.zh: 疆場之臣，肆為欺蔽，勝則張皇而言功，敗則掩覆而不言。

translations.literal: Border officials wantonly practiced deception; when victorious they exaggerated and spoke of merit; when defeated they concealed and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials brazenly deceived the court: when they won, they inflated their achievements; when they lost, they hid the truth and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 脫使乘上流之無備，為飲馬長江之謀，其誰與捍之？

translations.literal: If they should take advantage of the upper reaches' lack of preparation and plot to water their horses in the Yangtze, who would resist them?
translations.idiomatic: If they exploited our unpreparedness on the upper Yangtze and set their sights on watering their horses in the Long River, who could stop them?

sentences.zh: 是外患既深矣。

translations.literal: Thus external danger had already grown deep.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the external threat had already become grave.

sentences.zh: 人主上所事者天，下所恃者民。

translations.literal: For a ruler, what is served above is Heaven; what is relied upon below is the people.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler serves Heaven above and relies on the people below.

sentences.zh: 近者天文示變，妖彗吐芒，方冬而雷，既春而雪，海潮衝突於都城，赤地幾遍於畿甸，是不得乎天而天已怒矣。

translations.literal: Recently the heavens displayed anomalies: an evil comet shot its rays; there was thunder in deep winter and snow after spring had come; sea tides crashed against the capital; barren land spread nearly throughout the metropolitan region—thus Heaven was not obtained, and Heaven was already angry.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Heaven had shown its displeasure: an ill-omened comet blazed; thunder came in midwinter and snow after spring had begun; tidal surges battered the capital, and famine spread across the metropolitan region—Heaven's favor had been lost, and Heaven was already enraged.

sentences.zh: 人死於幹戈，死於饑饉，父子相棄，夫婦不相保，怨氣盈腹，謗言載路，“等死”一萌，何所不至，是不得乎民而民已怨矣。

translations.literal: People died from weapons, died from famine; fathers and sons abandoned one another; husbands and wives could not protect each other; resentment filled their bellies and slanders filled the roads; once the thought of "death is all the same" sprouted, what would not follow—thus the people were not obtained, and the people already resented.
translations.idiomatic: People died by the sword and by famine; fathers and sons cast one another aside; husbands and wives could not protect each other; resentment seethed and slander filled the roads—once the thought "death is all the same" took root, what limit could there be? The people's loyalty had been lost, and the people already nursed grievance.

sentences.zh: 內憂外患之交至，天心人心之俱失，陛下能與二三大臣安居於天下之上乎？

translations.literal: Internal worry and external danger arrived together; the mind of Heaven and the hearts of the people were both lost—could Your Majesty, together with two or three great ministers, dwell at ease above the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Internal crisis and external threat arrived together; Heaven's favor and the people's hearts were both lost—could Your Majesty, together with two or three great ministers, dwell at ease atop the realm?

sentences.zh: 陛下亦嚐思所以致此否乎？

translations.literal: Has Your Majesty also once reflected on what brought this about?
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty ever reflected on what brought this about?

sentences.zh: 蓋自曩者權相陽進妾婦之小忠，陰竊君人之大柄，以聲色玩好內蠱陛下之心術，而廢置生殺，一切惟其意之所欲為，以致紀綱陵夷，風俗頹靡，軍政不修而邊備廢缺。

translations.literal: It is because in times past the powerful minister openly advanced the petty loyalty of a concubine or wife, while secretly usurping the great authority of the ruler; with sound, color, and pleasures he inwardly poisoned Your Majesty's mind, while appointments, dismissals, life, and death were all at his whim—thus statutes collapsed, customs decayed, military administration was not repaired, and frontier defenses were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: It is because for years the powerful minister openly paraded petty loyalty while secretly seizing the ruler's great authority; with music, women, and luxuries he poisoned Your Majesty's mind, while appointments, dismissals, and matters of life and death all followed his whim—statutes collapsed, customs decayed, military affairs were neglected, and frontier defenses fell into ruin.

sentences.zh: 凡今日之內憂外患，皆權相三十年釀成之，如養護癰疽，待時而決耳。

translations.literal: All of today's internal worry and external danger were brewed over thirty years by the powerful minister, like nursing an abscess and waiting for the moment to lance it.
translations.idiomatic: All of today's internal crises and external threats were thirty years in the making by the powerful minister—like nursing an abscess until the moment came to lance it.

sentences.zh: 端平號為更化，而居相位者非其人，無能改於其舊，敗壞汙穢，殆有甚焉。

translations.literal: The Duanping era was called a renewal, yet the one occupying the chancellorship was not the right man; he could not change the old ways, and ruin and filth were perhaps even worse.
translations.idiomatic: The Duanping era was proclaimed a renewal, yet the man in the chancellorship was not the right one; he could not change the old ways, and corruption was perhaps even worse than before.

sentences.zh: 自是聖意惶惑，莫知所倚仗，方且不以彼為仇而以為德，不以彼為罪而以為功。

translations.literal: From this the sacred mind grew fearful and confused, not knowing whom to rely upon; yet he did not treat that man as an enemy but as a benefactor, did not treat him as guilty but as meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor's mind grew fearful and confused, not knowing whom to trust; yet he treated that man not as an enemy but as a benefactor, not as guilty but as meritorious.

sentences.zh: 於是天之望於陛下者孤，而變怪見矣，人之望於陛下者觖，而怨叛形矣。

translations.literal: Thus Heaven's hope in Your Majesty grew solitary, and strange omens appeared; the people's hope in Your Majesty grew disappointed, and resentment and rebellion took shape.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's hope in Your Majesty grew solitary, and omens of strangeness appeared; the people's hope in Your Majesty turned to disappointment, and resentment and rebellion took visible form.

sentences.zh: 陛下敬天有圖，旨酒有箴，緝熙有記，使持此一念，振起傾頹，宜無難者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty reveres Heaven with diagrams, has admonitions on strong wine, and records on bright cultivation—if you hold to this single thought and rouse what is toppling and failing, it should not be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reveres Heaven with ritual diagrams, has admonitions on strong wine, and records on bright cultivation—if you hold to this resolve and rouse what is toppling and failing, it should not be difficult.

sentences.zh: 然聞之道路，謂警懼之意，祗見於外朝視政之頃；

translations.literal: Yet it is heard on the roads that the spirit of vigilance appears only during the outer court's sessions of reviewing government;
translations.idiomatic: Yet word on the streets is that Your Majesty's vigilance appears only during outer-court sessions of reviewing government;

sentences.zh: 而好樂之私，多縱於內廷燕褻之際。

translations.literal: while the private love of pleasure is mostly indulged during intimate banquets in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: while the private love of pleasure is mostly indulged during intimate banquets in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 名為任賢，而左右近習或得而潛間；

translations.literal: It is called entrusting the worthy, yet attendants and close associates can secretly intervene;
translations.idiomatic: It is called entrusting affairs to the worthy, yet attendants and close associates can still intervene in secret;

sentences.zh: 政出於中書，而御筆特奏或從而中出。

translations.literal: government issues from the Secretariat, yet imperial brush memorials sometimes issue directly from the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: government issued from the Secretariat, yet imperial brush memorials sometimes came directly from the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 左道之蠱惑，私親之請托，蒙蔽陛下之聰明，轉移陛下之心術。

translations.literal: Heretical doctrines bewitch and delude; private requests and entreaties obscure Your Majesty's clarity and shift Your Majesty's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Heretical doctrines bewitched and deluded; private requests and entreaties obscured Your Majesty's clarity and shifted Your Majesty's mind.

sentences.zh: 於是範去國四載矣，帝撫勞備至。

translations.literal: Thus Fan had been away from the capital four years; the emperor comforted and rewarded him with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: By then Fan had been away from the capital four years; the emperor comforted and rewarded him with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 遷權吏部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to acting vice minister of personnel and concurrent lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 以久旱，復言：“陛下嗣膺寶位餘二十年，災異譴告，無歲無之，至於今而益甚。

translations.literal: Because of prolonged drought, he again spoke: "Your Majesty has borne the imperial throne for more than twenty years; calamities and strange omens rebuking and warning have occurred every year without fail, and this year they are worse than ever.
translations.idiomatic: Because of prolonged drought, he again spoke: "Your Majesty has borne the imperial throne for more than twenty years; calamities and strange omens rebuking and warning have occurred every year without fail—and this year they are worse than ever.

sentences.zh: 陛下求所以應天者，將止於減膳徹樂、分禱群祀而已乎？

translations.literal: When Your Majesty seeks how to respond to Heaven, will you stop at reducing meals, withdrawing music, and dividing prayers among the various sacrifices?
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty asks how to answer Heaven, will the answer stop at lighter meals, silenced music, and prayers scattered among many sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 抑當外此而反求諸躬乎？

translations.literal: Or should you go beyond this and turn to examine yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Or should you go beyond this and turn inward to examine yourself?

sentences.zh: 夫不務反躬悔過，而徒覬天怒之釋，天下寧有是理？

translations.literal: If one does not devote oneself to turning inward in repentance but merely hopes for Heaven's anger to be released, is there such a principle under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: If one does not devote oneself to turning inward in repentance but merely hopes for Heaven's anger to lift—is there such a principle under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 欲望陛下一灑舊習以新天下，出宮女以遠聲色，斥近習以防蔽欺，省浮費以給國用，薄征斂以寬民力。

translations.literal: I desire that Your Majesty sweep away old habits to renew the realm, send palace women away to keep sound and color at a distance, dismiss close associates to guard against concealment and deception, reduce wasteful expenditure to supply state needs, and lighten levies and exactions to ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to sweep away old habits to renew the realm, send palace women away to keep sound and color at a distance, dismiss close associates to guard against concealment and deception, reduce wasteful expenditure to supply state needs, and lighten levies and exactions to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 且儲貳未立，國本尚虛，乞選宗姓之賢者育之宮中而教導之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the heir apparent has not yet been established and the foundation of the state remains empty; I beg that a worthy member of the imperial clan be selected, reared in the palace, and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, no heir apparent has been named and the foundation of the state stands empty; I beg that a worthy member of the imperial clan be chosen, raised in the palace, and taught.

sentences.zh: ”又言銓法之壞：“廟堂既有堂除，復時取部缺以徇人情；

translations.literal: " He also spoke of the corruption of appointment regulations: "In the hall of government there are already direct appointments from the chancellor, yet vacancies in the ministry are also taken from time to time to gratify personal connections;
translations.idiomatic: " He also spoke of the corruption of appointment regulations: "In the hall of government there are already direct appointments from the chancellor, yet ministry vacancies are also taken from time to time to gratify personal connections;

sentences.zh: 士大夫既陷贓濫，乃間以不經推勘而改正。

translations.literal: when scholar-officials have fallen into corrupt excess, they are occasionally allowed to revise appointments through improper review.
translations.idiomatic: when scholar-officials have sunk into corrupt excess, they are sometimes allowed to revise appointments through improper review.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆徇私忘公之害。

translations.literal: All of these are the harm of favoring private interest and forgetting the public good.
translations.idiomatic: Each of these is the harm that comes of serving private interest and forgetting the public good.

sentences.zh: ”未幾，復上疏曰：

translations.literal: " Before long, he again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he again submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 天災旱暵，昔固有之。

translations.literal: Heavenly calamities of drought and heat have indeed existed in the past.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities of drought and scorching heat are nothing new.

sentences.zh: 而倉廩匱竭，月支不繼，升粟一千，其增未已，富戶淪落，十室九空，此又昔之所無也。

translations.literal: Yet granaries were exhausted and monthly disbursements could not continue; a sheng of grain cost a thousand cash, and the price kept rising; wealthy households fell into ruin, and nine of ten households stood empty—this is what the past never had.
translations.idiomatic: Yet granaries were exhausted and monthly disbursements could not continue; a sheng of grain cost a thousand cash, and the price kept rising; wealthy households fell into ruin, and nine of ten households stood empty—this the past never knew.

sentences.zh: 甚而闔門饑死，相率投江，裏巷聚首以議執政，軍伍誶語所不忍聞，此何等氣象，而見於京城眾大之區。

translations.literal: So extreme that whole households starved to death, people in succession threw themselves into the river, alleys gathered to discuss the administration, and in the camps there was foul language one could not bear to hear—what sort of atmosphere is this, seen in the great metropolitan region of the capital?
translations.idiomatic: It has reached the point where whole households starve to death, people throw themselves into the river one after another, alleys fill with talk against the administration, and in the camps there is language one cannot bear to hear—what kind of atmosphere is this, in the great capital itself?

sentences.zh: 浙西稻米所聚，而赤地千里。

translations.literal: Western Zhejiang is where rice is gathered, yet barren land stretched a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhejiang is where rice is gathered, yet for a thousand li the land lay bare.

sentences.zh: 淮民流離，繈負相屬，欲歸無所，奄奄待盡。

translations.literal: Huai people wandered in exile, carrying infants on their backs in unbroken lines, wishing to return yet having nowhere to go, gasping out their last breaths as they waited to die.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from the Huai wandered in endless lines, infants on their backs, longing to return but with nowhere to go, gasping out their last breaths as they waited to die.

sentences.zh: 使邊塵不起，尚可相依苟活，萬一敵騎衝突，彼必奔迸南來，或相攜從敵，因為之鄉導，巴蜀之覆轍可鑒也。

translations.literal: If frontier dust did not rise, they could still depend on one another and live miserably; but if enemy cavalry should suddenly strike, they would surely flee south in panic, or even go over to the enemy together and serve as their guides—the lesson of Ba-Shu's ruin can be taken as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: If the frontier remained quiet, they could still depend on one another and scrape by; but if enemy cavalry should suddenly strike, they would surely flee south in panic, or even go over to the enemy together and serve as their guides—the lesson of Ba-Shu's ruin stands as a warning.

sentences.zh: 竊意陛下宵旰憂懼，寧處弗遑。

translations.literal: I privately think Your Majesty stays up late and rises early in worry and fear, with no leisure even to rest.
translations.idiomatic: I imagine Your Majesty rising early and staying up late in worry and fear, with scarcely a moment's rest.

sentences.zh: 然宮中宴賜未聞有所貶損，左右嬙嬖未聞有所放遣，貂璫近習未聞有所斥遠，女冠請謁未聞有所屏絕，朝廷政事未聞有所修飭，庶府積蠹未聞有所搜革。

translations.literal: Yet I have not heard that palace banquets and rewards have been reduced, that attendants and favorites have been dismissed, that eunuchs and close associates have been driven away, that requests for audience from female Daoist priests have been barred, that court governance has been rectified, or that accumulated corruption in the various offices has been searched out and reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear of no reduction in palace banquets and rewards, no dismissal of attendants and favorites, no driving away of eunuchs and close associates, no barring of female Daoist priests who seek audience, no rectification of court governance, and no searching out of accumulated corruption in the various offices.

sentences.zh: 秉國鈞者惟私情之徇，主道揆者惟法守之侵，國家大政則相持而不決，司存細務則出意而輒行。

translations.literal: Those holding the state's balance yield only to private feeling; those directing policy encroach only upon the observance of law; great state policies are held in stalemate without decision, while minor departmental affairs are carried out at whim.
translations.idiomatic: Those holding the state's balance yield only to private feeling; those directing policy encroach only upon the observance of law; great state policies stall without decision, while minor departmental affairs are carried out at whim.

sentences.zh: 命令朝更而夕變，紀綱蕩廢而不存，無一事之不弊，無一弊之不極。

translations.literal: Orders change morning and evening; statutes are swept away and no longer exist; there is nothing that is not corrupt, and no corruption that does not reach its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Orders change from morning to evening; statutes are swept away until none remain; nothing is free of corruption, and every corruption has reached its extreme.

sentences.zh: 陛下盍亦震懼自省。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should also be shaken into fear and turn to self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to be shaken to fear and turn inward in self-examination.

sentences.zh: 詔：“中外臣庶思當今急務，如河道未通，軍餉若何而可運？

translations.literal: An edict said: "Officials and commoners within and without should think on today's urgent tasks: if the canal route is not open, how can army provisions be transported?
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed: "Officials and commoners within and without should ponder today's urgent tasks—if the canal route is not open, how are army provisions to be moved?

sentences.zh: 浙右旱歉，荒政若何而可行？

translations.literal: Eastern Zhejiang suffers drought and poor harvest—how can famine relief be carried out?
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhejiang suffers drought and poor harvest—by what means can famine relief be carried out?

sentences.zh: 財計空匱，糴本若何而可足？

translations.literal: The treasury is empty—how can funds for grain purchases be secured?
translations.idiomatic: The treasury stands empty—how can funds for grain purchases be secured?

sentences.zh: 流徙失所，遣使若何而可定？

translations.literal: The displaced have lost their homes—how can envoys be dispatched to settle them?
translations.idiomatic: The displaced have lost their homes—how can envoys be sent to settle them?

sentences.zh: 敵情叵測，邊圉若何而可固？

translations.literal: The enemy's intentions are hard to fathom—how can the frontier be secured?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's intentions are impossible to read—how can the frontier be made secure?

sentences.zh: 各務悉力盡思，以陳持危製變之策。

translations.literal: Each should exert full effort and thought to set forth policies for holding crisis and controlling change.
translations.idiomatic: Let each exert every effort and every thought to set forth policies for holding crisis and mastering change.

sentences.zh: 拜吏部侍郎兼中書舍人，復極言宴賜不節、修造不時、玩寇縱欲數事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, and again spoke forcefully on several matters: unrestrained banquets and rewards, untimely construction, indulging the enemy and yielding to desire.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of personnel and concurrent drafting attendant of the Secretariat, and again spoke forcefully on several matters: unrestrained banquets and rewards, untimely construction, indulging the enemy and yielding to desire.

sentences.zh: 兼權兵部尚書，改禮部尚書兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Acting Minister of War, then was changed to Minister of Rites and concurrent Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as acting minister of war, then was changed to minister of rites and concurrent drafting attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，擢同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunyou he was promoted to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunyou he was promoted to associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 範既入都堂，凡行事有得失，除授有是非，悉抗言無隱情。

translations.literal: Once Fan entered the chief council, in every action whether there was gain or loss, and in every appointment whether there was right or wrong, he remonstrated without concealing his views.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fan entered the chief council, whether an action brought gain or loss, whether an appointment was right or wrong, he spoke out without hiding his views.

sentences.zh: 丞相史嵩之外示寬容，內實忌之。

translations.literal: The Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi outwardly showed tolerance but inwardly in fact resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillor Shi Songzhi outwardly showed tolerance but inwardly resented him.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以李鳴復參知政事，範不屑與鳴復共政，去之。

translations.literal: When Li Mingfu was appointed Vice Grand Councillor, Fan disdained to serve in government with Mingfu and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mingfu was appointed vice grand councillor, Fan disdained to serve in government with Mingfu and left.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中使召回，且敕諸城門不得出範。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to recall him and also ordered that none of the city gates should let Fan out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to recall him and ordered that none of the city gates should let Fan out.

sentences.zh: 太學諸生亦上書留範而斥鳴復，並斥嵩之。

translations.literal: Students of the Imperial Academy also submitted memorials to keep Fan and denounce Mingfu, and also denounced Songzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Imperial Academy also submitted memorials asking that Fan be kept and Mingfu denounced—and Songzhi as well.

sentences.zh: 嵩之令諫議大夫劉晉之等論範及鳴復，範遂行。

translations.literal: Songzhi had Remonstrance Official Liu Jinzhi and others criticize Fan and Mingfu, and Fan then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi had remonstrance official Liu Jinzhi and others criticize Fan and Mingfu, and Fan then departed.

sentences.zh: 會嵩之遭喪謀起復不果，於是拜範右丞相，範以遜遊似，不許，遂力疾入覲。

translations.literal: When Songzhi, encountering bereavement, plotted to resume office but failed, Fan was then appointed Right Chief Councillor; Fan yielded to You Yousi, which was not permitted, and so he forced himself to attend audience despite illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Songzhi, encountering bereavement, plotted to resume office but failed, Fan was then appointed right chief councillor; Fan yielded to You Yousi, which was not permitted, and so he forced himself to attend audience despite illness.

sentences.zh: 帝親書“開誠心，布公道。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote "Open the sincere heart and spread impartial justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in his own hand, "Open the sincere heart and spread impartial justice.

sentences.zh: 集眾思，廣忠益”賜之。

translations.literal: Gather all counsel and broaden loyal benefit" and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gather all counsel and broaden loyal benefit," and bestowed it upon him.

sentences.zh: 範上五事：“曰正治本，謂政事當常出於中書，毋使旁蹊得竊威福。

translations.literal: Fan submitted five matters: "First, rectify the root of governance—meaning that government affairs should regularly issue from the Secretariat, and side paths must not steal authority and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan submitted five matters: "First, rectify the root of governance—government affairs should regularly issue from the Secretariat, and side paths must not steal authority and blessing.

sentences.zh: 曰肅宮闈，謂當嚴內外之限，使宮府一體。

translations.literal: Second, rectify the inner palace—meaning that the boundary between inner and outer should be strict, so that palace and government form one body.
translations.idiomatic: Second, rectify the inner palace—the boundary between inner and outer should be strict, so that palace and government form one body.

sentences.zh: 曰擇人才，謂當隨其所長用之而久於職，毋徒守遷轉之常格。

translations.literal: Third, select talent—meaning that each should be employed according to his strengths and kept long in office, not merely bound by the regular rules of transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Third, select talent—each should be employed according to his strengths and kept long in office, not merely bound by the regular rules of transfer.

sentences.zh: 曰惜名器，謂如文臣貼職，武臣閣衛，不當為徇私市恩之地。

translations.literal: Fourth, cherish titles and offices—meaning that such posts as honorary civil titles and guard posts for military officers should not become places for favoring private interest and trading in grace.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, cherish titles and offices—such posts as honorary civil titles and guard posts for military officers should not become places for favoring private interest and trading in grace.

sentences.zh: 曰節財用，謂當自人主一身始，自宮掖始，自貴近始，考封村國用出入之數，而補窒其罅漏，求鹽策楮幣變更之目，而斟酌其利害。

translations.literal: Fifth, economize state expenditure—meaning that this should begin with the ruler himself, with the inner palace, and with the honored and close; examine the figures of income and outgo for enfeoffments and state use, and mend the cracks and leaks; seek the items for changing salt policy and paper currency, and weigh their benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, economize state expenditure—this should begin with the ruler himself, with the inner palace, and with the honored and close; examine the figures of income and outgo for enfeoffments and state use, and mend the cracks and leaks; seek the items for changing salt policy and paper currency, and weigh their benefits and harms.

sentences.zh: 仍乞早定國本以係人心。

translations.literal: I still beg that the foundation of the state be settled early to bind the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: I still beg that the foundation of the state be settled early, so as to bind the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 時親王近戚多求降恩澤，引前朝杜衍例，範皆封還。

translations.literal: At the time many imperial princes and close kin sought lowered favors, citing the precedent of Du Yan of the former dynasty; Fan returned them all sealed.
translations.idiomatic: Many imperial princes and close kin at the time sought lowered favors, citing the precedent of Du Yan in the former dynasty; Fan returned every petition sealed.

sentences.zh: 乞撥堂除闕歸之吏部，以清中書之務，惟留書庫、架閣、京教及要地幹官。

translations.literal: He requested that direct appointments from the chancellor's office be returned to the Ministry of Personnel to clarify the Secretariat's affairs, retaining only posts for archive clerks, shelf officials, capital instructors, and key executive posts.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that direct appointments from the chancellor's office be returned to the Ministry of Personnel, to clarify the Secretariat's work, retaining only archive clerks, shelf officials, capital instructors, and key executive posts.

sentences.zh: 人皆以為不便。

translations.literal: People all thought it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: People all thought it inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 太學生亦上書言之，帝以示範，範奏曰：“三四十年權臣柄國，以公朝爵祿而市私恩，取吏部之闕以歸堂除，太學諸生亦習於見聞，乃以近年之弊政為祖宗之成法。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy students also submitted memorials on the matter; the emperor showed this to Fan, and Fan memorialized: "For three or four decades powerful ministers held the state, using public court rank and salary to trade in private favor, taking ministry vacancies for direct chancellor appointment—Imperial Academy students too have grown accustomed to what they see and hear, and now treat recent corrupt policies as the established laws of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy students also memorialized on the matter; the emperor showed this to Fan, and Fan wrote: "For three or four decades powerful ministers held the state, trading public rank and salary for private favor, taking ministry vacancies for direct chancellor appointment—and Academy students, accustomed to what they see and hear, now treat recent corrupt policies as the ancestors' established law.

sentences.zh: 如以臣言為是，上下堅守，則諛者必多而謗者息矣。

translations.literal: If my words are accepted as right and upheld above and below, then flatterers will surely multiply and slanderers will cease.
translations.idiomatic: If my words are accepted as right and upheld above and below, flatterers will surely multiply and slanderers fall silent.

sentences.zh: ”未幾，赴選調者無淹滯，合資格者得美闕，眾始服。

translations.literal: " Before long, those going for selection and transfer suffered no delay; those meeting qualifications obtained fine posts, and the multitude then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long those going for selection and transfer met no delay; those who qualified obtained fine posts, and the multitude at last submitted.

sentences.zh: 帝命宰執各條當今利病與政事可行者，範上十二事：

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chief ministers each to set forth current benefits and harms and feasible policies; Fan submitted twelve matters:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chief ministers each to set forth current benefits and harms and policies that could be carried out; Fan submitted twelve matters:

sentences.zh: 曰公用舍，願進退人才悉參以國人之論，則乘罅抵巇者無所投其間。

translations.literal: First, public employment and dismissal—may advancement and removal of talent all be referred to public opinion, so that those who exploit cracks and crevices will have no place to insert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: First, public employment and dismissal—let advancement and removal of talent be guided by public opinion, so that those who exploit every crack and crevice have no opening.

sentences.zh: 曰儲材能，內而朝列，則儲宰執於侍從、台諫，儲侍從、台諫於卿監、郎官；

translations.literal: Second, store talent and ability—within the court, store chief ministers among attendants and remonstrance officials; store attendants and remonstrance officials among directors, supervisors, and department officials;
translations.idiomatic: Second, store talent and ability—within the court, groom chief ministers from among attendants and remonstrance officials; groom attendants and remonstrance officials from among directors, supervisors, and department officials;

sentences.zh: 外而守帥，則以江麵之通判為幕府、郡守之儲，以江麵之郡守為帥閫之儲；

translations.literal: without, among prefects and commanders, take Jiang region vice-prefects as reserves for staff and prefects, and Jiang region prefects as reserves for commanders;
translations.idiomatic: without, among prefects and commanders, let Jiang-region vice-prefects serve as reserves for staff and prefects, and Jiang-region prefects as reserves for commanders;

sentences.zh: 他職皆然，如是則臨時無乏才之憂。

translations.literal: other offices are likewise—thus at the moment there will be no worry of lacking talent.
translations.idiomatic: the same for other offices—thus there will be no fear of lacking talent when the moment comes.

sentences.zh: 曰嚴薦舉，宜詔中外之臣，凡薦舉必明著職業、功狀、事實，不許止為褒詞，朝廷籍記不如所舉，並罰舉主，仍詔侍從、台諫不許與人覓舉。

translations.literal: Third, strict recommendations—an edict should be issued to officials within and without: every recommendation must clearly state office, achievements, and facts; mere praise is not permitted; if the court's records do not match what was recommended, the recommender is also punished; further, attendants and remonstrance officials are forbidden to seek recommendations for others.
translations.idiomatic: Third, strict recommendations—let an edict go out to officials within and without: every recommendation must clearly state office, achievements, and facts; mere praise will not do; if the court's records do not match what was recommended, the recommender is punished as well; and attendants and remonstrance officials must not seek recommendations for others.

sentences.zh: 曰懲贓貪，自今有以贓罪案上，即行下勘證，果有贓敗，必繩以祖宗之法，無實跡而監司妄以贓罪誣人者，亦量行責罰，台諫風聞言及贓罪，亦行下勘證。

translations.literal: Fourth, punish corruption—in future when a bribery case is submitted, it should immediately be sent down for investigation; if corruption is truly found, the laws of the ancestors must be applied; if there is no real evidence yet a surveillance commissioner falsely accuses someone of bribery, he too should receive measured punishment; if remonstrance officials hear of bribery and speak of it, investigation should also be sent down.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, punish corruption—from now on when a bribery case is submitted, send it down at once for investigation; if corruption is truly found, apply the laws of the ancestors; if a surveillance commissioner falsely accuses someone without real evidence, he too receives measured punishment; and when remonstrance officials hear of bribery and speak of it, investigation must also be sent down.

sentences.zh: 曰專職任，吏部不可兼給、舍，京尹不可兼戶、吏，經筵亦必專官。

translations.literal: Fifth, exclusive duties—the Ministry of Personnel must not concurrently hold posts of provision and drafting; the capital magistrate must not concurrently hold posts of revenue and personnel; the lecture circuit must also have dedicated officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, exclusive duties—the Ministry of Personnel must not concurrently hold provision and drafting posts; the capital magistrate must not concurrently hold revenue and personnel posts; the lecture circuit, too, must have dedicated officials.

sentences.zh: 曰久任使，內而財賦、獄訟、銓選與其他煩劇之職，必三年而後遷，外而監司、郡守，亦必使之再任，其不能者則亟行罷斥。

translations.literal: Sixth, long tenure—within, for finance, litigation, selection, and other arduous duties, transfer must come only after three years; without, for surveillance commissioners and prefects, they must also be made to serve a second term; those who cannot do so should quickly be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, long tenure—within the court, for finance, litigation, selection, and other arduous duties, transfer must come only after three years; without, for surveillance commissioners and prefects, they must also be made to serve a second term; those who cannot do so should quickly be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 曰抑僥幸，布告中外，各務職業，朝廷不以弊例而過恩，宮庭不以私謁而廢法；

translations.literal: Seventh, restrain undeserved favor—proclaim this within and without: each should attend to his office; the court must not grant excessive grace through corrupt precedents; the palace must not set aside law through private requests;
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, restrain undeserved favor—proclaim within and without that each should attend to his office; the court must not grant excessive grace through corrupt precedents; the palace must not set aside law for private requests;

sentences.zh: 勳舊之家，邸第之戚，不以名器而輕假。

translations.literal: meritorious old families and kin of great houses must not lightly be given titles and offices.
translations.idiomatic: meritorious old families and kin of great houses must not be lightly given titles and offices.

sentences.zh: 曰重閫寄。

translations.literal: Eighth, value frontier command.
