translations.idiomatic: Eighth, value frontier command.

sentences.zh: 曰選軍實。

translations.literal: Ninth, select real military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, select real military strength.

sentences.zh: 曰招土豪。

translations.literal: Tenth, recruit local strongmen.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, recruit local strongmen.

sentences.zh: 曰宜仿祖宗方田之製，疏為溝洫，縱橫經緯，各相灌注，以鑿溝之土，積而為徑，使不得並轡而馳，結陣而前，如曹瑋守陝西之製，則戎馬之來，所至皆有阻限，而溝之內又可以耕屯，勝於陸地多矣。

translations.literal: Eleventh, it is suitable to follow the ancestral square-field system, dredge canals and ditches in crisscross grid, each irrigating the other; use the earth dug from the ditches piled into paths, so that horses cannot ride abreast and charge, and formations cannot advance together—like Cao Wei's defense of Shaanxi—then when barbarian horses come, wherever they reach there will be obstacles and limits, and within the ditches one can also farm and garrison, far better than open land.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh, follow the ancestral square-field system: dredge canals and ditches in a crisscross grid, each channel feeding the next; pile the earth dug from the ditches into paths so horses cannot ride abreast or charge, and formations cannot advance together—as Cao Wei did in defending Shaanxi—so that when barbarian horses come, wherever they reach they meet obstacles and limits, and within the ditches one can farm and garrison, far better than open ground.

sentences.zh: 曰治邊、理財，實為當今急務，有明於治邊、善於理財者，搜訪以聞。

translations.literal: Twelfth, governing the frontier and managing finances are truly today's urgent tasks; those clear about frontier governance and skilled in managing finances should be sought out and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, governing the frontier and managing finances are truly the urgent tasks of the day; those skilled in frontier governance and in managing finances should be sought out and reported.

sentences.zh: 時孟珙權重兵久居上流，朝廷素疑其難製，至是以書來賀。

translations.literal: At the time Meng Gong had long held heavy troops on the upper reaches; the court had always suspected he would be hard to control; now he sent a letter of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Gong had long held heavy troops on the upper reaches; the court had always suspected he would prove hard to control; now he sent a letter of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 範復之曰：“古人謂將相調和則士豫附，自此但相與同心徇國。

translations.literal: Fan replied: "The ancients said that when generals and ministers are in harmony, soldiers gladly attach themselves; from now on let us only join hearts in serving the state.
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied: "The ancients said that when generals and ministers are in harmony, soldiers gladly attach themselves; from this day let us join hearts in serving the state alone.

sentences.zh: 若以術相籠架，非範所屑為也。

translations.literal: If one uses stratagems to cage and constrain each other, that is not what Fan would stoop to.
translations.idiomatic: If we use stratagems to cage and constrain each other, that is beneath Fan's dignity.

sentences.zh: ”珙大感服。

translations.literal: " Gong was deeply moved and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Gong was deeply moved and submitted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大元軍大入五河，絕中流，置營柵，且以重兵綴合肥，令不得相援，為必取壽春之計。

translations.literal: Before long, the Great Yuan army entered deeply into the Five Rivers, cut the midstream, set up camp palisades, and with heavy troops pinned down Hefei so that forces could not support one another, planning to take Shouchun for certain.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Great Yuan army poured deep into the Five Rivers, cut the midstream, erected camp palisades, and pinned down Hefei with heavy troops so that forces could not aid one another, planning to take Shouchun without fail.

sentences.zh: 範命惟揚、鄂渚二帥各調兵東西來應，卒以捷聞。

translations.literal: Fan ordered the two commanders of Weiyang and Ezhu each to mobilize troops from east and west to respond; in the end victory was reported.
translations.idiomatic: Fan ordered the commanders of Weiyang and Ezhu each to mobilize troops from east and west; in the end victory was reported.

sentences.zh: 範計功行賞，莫不曲當，軍士皆悅。

translations.literal: Fan assessed merit and distributed rewards; none was inappropriate, and the soldiers were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fan assessed merit and distributed rewards, and every award was fitting; the soldiers were all pleased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，贈少傅，諡清獻。

translations.literal: Before long he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor and given the posthumous title Qingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as junior tutor and given the posthumous title Qingxian.

sentences.zh: 其所著述，有古律詩歌詞五卷，雜文六卷，奏稿十卷，外製三卷，《進故事》五卷，《經筵講義》三卷。

translations.literal: His writings included five juan of regulated verse, songs, and lyrics; six juan of miscellaneous prose; ten juan of memorial drafts; three juan of external compositions; five juan of Record of Presented Affairs; and three juan of Lectures for the Lecture Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Among his writings were five juan of regulated verse, songs, and lyrics; six juan of miscellaneous prose; ten juan of memorial drafts; three juan of external compositions; five juan of Record of Presented Affairs; and three juan of Lectures for the Lecture Circuit.

sentences.zh: 楊簡，字敬仲，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Yang Jian, styled Jingzhong, was a man of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian, whose courtesy name was Jingzhong, came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年舉進士，授富陽主簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao year five he passed the jinshi examination and received appointment as chief clerk of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 會陸九淵道過富陽，問答有所契，遂定師弟子之禮。

translations.literal: When Lu Jiuyuan passed through Fuyang, in question and answer they found agreement, and he then fixed the rites of master and disciple.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Jiuyuan passed through Fuyang, their questions and answers found accord, and he thereupon established the rites of master and disciple.

sentences.zh: 富陽民多服賈而不知學，簡興學養士，文風益振。

translations.literal: The people of Fuyang mostly engaged in trade and did not know learning; Jian raised schools and nurtured scholars, and literary culture flourished the more.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fuyang mostly engaged in trade and knew little of learning; Jian raised schools and nurtured scholars, and literary culture flourished the more.

sentences.zh: 為紹興府司理，犴獄必親臨，端默以聽，使自吐露。

translations.literal: Serving as judicial officer of Shaoxing Prefecture, he always personally attended the prison himself, sitting in silence to listen and letting prisoners speak for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as judicial officer of Shaoxing Prefecture, he always personally attended the prison, sitting in silence to listen and letting prisoners speak for themselves.

sentences.zh: 越陪都，台府鼎立，簡中平無頗，惟理之從。

translations.literal: Yue was the secondary capital; the surveillance and prefectural offices stood like a tripod; Jian was impartial without bias and followed only what was right.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was the secondary capital, where surveillance and prefectural offices stood like a tripod; Jian held the center without bias and followed only what was right.

sentences.zh: 一府史觸怒帥，令鞫之，簡白無罪，命鞫平日，簡曰：“吏過詎能免，今日實無罪，必擿往事置之法，某不敢奉命。

translations.literal: A clerk of the prefecture angered the commander; the commander ordered him interrogated; Jian declared him innocent; the commander ordered his past conduct interrogated; Jian said: "A clerk's faults surely cannot be avoided, but today he is truly innocent; if you must dredge up past matters to punish him by law, I dare not obey the order.
translations.idiomatic: A prefectural clerk angered the commander, who ordered him interrogated; Jian declared him innocent; the commander ordered his past conduct examined; Jian said: "A clerk's faults cannot be avoided, but today he is truly innocent; if you must dredge up old matters to punish him by law, I dare not obey.

sentences.zh: ”帥大怒，簡取告身納之，爭愈力。

translations.literal: " The commander was greatly angered; Jian took his commission and submitted it, and argued all the more forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: " The commander flew into a rage; Jian handed in his commission and argued all the harder.

sentences.zh: 常平使者朱熹薦之。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Zhu Xi recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Zhu Xi recommended him.

sentences.zh: 先是，丞相史浩亦以簡薦，差浙西撫幹，白尹張枃，宜因凶歲戒不虞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chief Councillor Shi Hao had also recommended Jian; he was assigned as pacification staff officer in western Zhejiang and informed Magistrate Zhang Kan that because it was a famine year one should guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, chief councillor Shi Hao had also recommended Jian; he was assigned as pacification staff officer in western Zhejiang and informed Magistrate Zhang Kan that because it was a famine year one should guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 乃令簡督三將兵，接以恩信，出諸葛亮正兵法肄習之，軍政大修，眾大和悅。

translations.literal: He then had Jian supervise three generals' troops, receiving them with grace and trust, drilling them in Zhuge Liang's orthodox military methods; military administration was greatly improved and the multitude was harmonious and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Jian supervise the troops of three generals, receiving them with grace and trust and drilling them in Zhuge Liang's orthodox military methods; military administration was greatly improved, and the troops were harmonious and pleased.

sentences.zh: 改知嵊縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Sheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to magistrate of Sheng County.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，服除，知樂平縣，興學訓士，諸生聞其言有泣下者。

translations.literal: Upon the death of his father he mourned; when mourning ended he became magistrate of Leping County, raised schools and trained scholars, and among the students some wept upon hearing his words.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father's death he became magistrate of Leping County, raised schools and trained scholars, and some among the students wept upon hearing his words.

sentences.zh: 楊、石二少年為民害，簡置獄中，諭以禍福，鹹感悟，願自贖。

translations.literal: Two youths, Yang and Shi, were a harm to the people; Jian placed them in prison, admonished them on fortune and disaster, and both were moved and wished to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Two youths, Yang and Shi, were a plague upon the people; Jian imprisoned them, admonished them on fortune and disaster, and both were moved and wished to redeem themselves.

sentences.zh: 由是邑人以訟為恥，夜無盜警，路不拾遺。

translations.literal: From this the people of the district took litigation as shameful; at night there were no theft alarms; on the roads nothing lost was picked up.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the people of the district took litigation as shameful; at night there were no alarms of theft; on the roads no one picked up what another had lost.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年，召為國子博士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxi he was summoned as Doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxi he was summoned as doctor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 二少年大帥縣民隨出境外，呼曰“楊父”。

translations.literal: The two youths led county people to follow him beyond the border, calling out "Father Yang."
translations.idiomatic: The two youths led county people after him beyond the border, calling out, "Father Yang!"

sentences.zh: 會斥丞相趙汝愚，祭酒李祥抗章辨之，簡上書言：“昨者危急，軍民將潰亂，社稷將傾危，陛下所親見。

translations.literal: When Chief Councillor Zhao Ruyu was dismissed, Libationer Li Xiang submitted a forceful memorial in his defense; Jian submitted a memorial saying: "In the recent crisis, the army and people were about to fall into disorder, and the altars of state were about to topple—Your Majesty saw this with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When chief councillor Zhao Ruyu was dismissed, libationer Li Xiang submitted a forceful memorial in his defense; Jian submitted a memorial saying: "In the recent crisis, the army and people were about to fall into disorder, and the altars of state were about to topple—Your Majesty saw this with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 汝愚冒萬死易危為安，人情妥定，汝愚之忠，陛下所心知，不必深辨。

translations.literal: Ruyu braved ten thousand deaths to turn danger into safety; popular feeling was settled; Ruyu's loyalty Your Majesty knows in your heart—there is no need for deep argument.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu braved ten thousand deaths to turn danger into safety; the people's hearts were settled; Your Majesty knows Ruyu's loyalty in your heart—there is no need to argue the point at length.

sentences.zh: 臣為祭酒屬，日以義訓諸生，若見利忘義，畏害忘義，臣恥之。

translations.literal: As libationer I daily instruct the students with righteousness; if I saw profit and forgot righteousness, or feared harm and forgot righteousness, I would be ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: As libationer I daily instruct the students in righteousness; to see profit and forget righteousness, or to fear harm and forget righteousness—that I would be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: ”未幾，亦遭斥，主管崇道觀。

translations.literal: " Before long he too was dismissed and put in charge of Chongdao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he, too, was dismissed and placed in charge of Chongdao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 再任，轉朝奉郎。

translations.literal: On a second appointment he was transferred to Gentleman for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: On a second appointment he was transferred to gentleman for court audience.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰四年，賜緋衣銀魚，朝散郎，權發遣全州，以言罷，主管仙都觀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiatai he was granted scarlet robes and silver fish, Gentleman for Dispersed Duty, and temporarily dispatched to Quanzhou; because of his memorial he was dismissed and put in charge of Xiandu Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiatai he was granted scarlet robes and silver fish, gentleman for dispersed duty, and temporarily dispatched to Quanzhou; because of his memorial he was dismissed and put in charge of Xiandu Abbey.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，寧宗更化，授秘書郎，轉朝請郎，遷秘書省著作佐郎兼權兵部郎官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading, when Emperor Ningzong renewed governance, he was appointed Secretary Gentleman, transferred to Gentleman for Court Service, and promoted to Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat and concurrent Acting Military Department Official.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading, when Emperor Ningzong renewed governance, he was appointed secretary gentleman, transferred to gentleman for court service, and promoted to assistant compiler in the Secretariat and concurrent acting military department official.

sentences.zh: 轉對，極言經國之要，弭災厲、消禍變之道，北境傳誦，為之涕泣。

translations.literal: At the rotating audience he spoke forcefully on essentials of governing the state and ways to quell calamities and dispel portents; north of the border his words were copied and passed around, and people wept over them.
translations.idiomatic: At the rotating audience he spoke forcefully on the essentials of governing the state and on ways to quell calamities and dispel portents; north of the border his words were copied and passed hand to hand, and people wept over them.

sentences.zh: 詔以旱蝗求直言，簡上封事，言旱蝗根本，近在人心。

translations.literal: An edict sought forthright speech because of drought and locusts; Jian submitted a sealed memorial saying the root of drought and locusts lay close at hand in the human heart.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sought forthright speech because of drought and locusts; Jian submitted a sealed memorial declaring that the root of drought and locusts lay close at hand—in the human heart.

sentences.zh: 兼考功郎官，兼禮部郎官，授著作郎、將作少監。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Merit Officer and Rites Department Official, and was appointed Compiler and Assistant Director of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as merit officer and rites department official, and was appointed compiler and assistant director of palace buildings.

sentences.zh: 入對，答問往復，漏過八刻，上目送久之。

translations.literal: He entered for audience; question and answer went back and forth until the eighth quarter after the water clock; the emperor gazed after him a long time as he departed.
translations.idiomatic: He entered for audience; question and answer went back and forth until the eighth quarter of the water clock had passed; the emperor watched him depart for a long while.

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官兼實錄院檢討官，以麵對所陳未行，求外補，知溫州。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Compiler of the National History Office and Examiner of the Veritable Records Office; because what he had stated at audience was not implemented, he sought an outside post and became prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as compiler of the National History Office and examiner of the Veritable Records Office; because what he had stated at audience was not implemented, he sought an outside post and became prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 移文首罷妓籍，尊敬賢士。

translations.literal: In his opening dispatch he first abolished the registry of courtesans and honored worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: His opening dispatch first abolished the registry of courtesans and gave honor to worthy men.

sentences.zh: 私鹺五百為群過境內，分司幹官檄永嘉尉及水砦兵捕之。

translations.literal: Five hundred piculs of private salt passed through the district in a group; the branch office staff official ordered the Yongjia district magistrate and river-fort soldiers to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred piculs of private salt passed through the district in a band; the branch-office staff official ordered the Yongjia district magistrate and river-fort soldiers to capture them.

sentences.zh: 巡尉不白郡，簡驚曰：“是可輕動乎？

translations.literal: The patrol officer did not inform the prefecture; Jian said in alarm: "Can this be lightly set in motion?
translations.idiomatic: The patrol officer had not informed the prefecture; Jian said in alarm: "Can this be set in motion so lightly?

sentences.zh: 萬一召亂，貽朝廷憂。

translations.literal: If disorder is summoned by chance, it will bring worry to the court.
translations.idiomatic: If by chance disorder is summoned, it will bring grief to the court.

sentences.zh: 兵之節製在郡將，違節製是不嚴天子命，違節製應斬。

translations.literal: Military restraint lies with the prefectural commander; violating restraint is not strictly obeying the Son of Heaven's command, and violating restraint should be punished by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Military restraint belongs to the prefectural commander; to violate restraint is to fail strictly to obey the Son of Heaven's command, and violation of restraint merits decapitation.

sentences.zh: ”建旗立巡尉庭下，召劊手兩行夾立，郡官盛服立西序，數其罪，命斬之，郡官交進為致悔罪意，良久得釋，奏罷分司，其紀律如此。

translations.literal: " He raised a banner and set up the patrol officer in the court below, summoned executioners in two rows standing on either side, had prefectural officials in full dress stand in the western row, counted his crimes, and ordered decapitation; prefectural officials came forward in turn to plead for repentance; after a long time he was released; he memorialized to dismiss the branch office—such was his discipline.
translations.idiomatic: " He raised a banner and placed the patrol officer in the court below, summoned executioners in two rows on either side, had prefectural officials in full dress stand in the western row, counted out his crimes, and ordered decapitation; prefectural officials came forward one after another to plead repentance; after a long while he was released; he memorialized to dismiss the branch office—such was his discipline.

sentences.zh: 寓官置民田負其直，簡追其隸責之而償所負。

translations.literal: An official on temporary assignment had commoners' fields registered in his name while owing their price; Jian pursued his subordinates, held them responsible, and repaid what was owed.
translations.idiomatic: A temporary official had commoners' fields registered in his name while owing their price; Jian pursued his subordinates, held them responsible, and repaid what was owed.

sentences.zh: 勢家第宅障官河，即日撤之，城中歡踴，名楊公河。

translations.literal: Powerful families' mansions blocked the official river; he demolished them the same day; the city rejoiced and leaped, and the river was named Lord Yang's River.
translations.idiomatic: Mansions of powerful families blocked the official river; he demolished them the same day; the city erupted in joy, and the river was named Lord Yang's River.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使至郡譏察，使於簡為先世契，出郊迎，不敢當，從間道走州入客位。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to the prefecture to inspect and censure; the envoy was an old family associate of Jian's; Jian went out to the suburbs to welcome him but did not dare accept the honor and went by a side path to enter the guest hall of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to inspect and censure the prefecture; the envoy was an old family associate of Jian's; Jian went out to the suburbs to welcome him but did not dare accept the honor and took a side path into the prefecture's guest hall.

sentences.zh: 簡聞之不敢入，往來傳送數四，乃驅車反。

translations.literal: When Jian heard of it he did not dare enter; messages were sent back and forth four times, and then he drove back.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian heard of this he did not dare enter; messages shuttled back and forth four times, and then he turned his carriage back.

sentences.zh: 將降車，使者趨出立戟門外，簡亦趨出立使者外，頓首言曰：“天使也，某不敢不肅。

translations.literal: As he was about to descend from the carriage, the envoy hurried out and stood outside the halberd gate; Jian also hurried out and stood outside the envoy, bowed his head and said: "An imperial envoy— I dare not fail to be reverent.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to step down from the carriage, the envoy hurried out and stood beyond the halberd gate; Jian hurried out too and stood beyond the envoy, bowed low, and said: "An imperial envoy—I dare not fail in reverence.

sentences.zh: ”使者曰：“契家子，禮有常尊。

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "We are family by old ties; ritual has its constant honor.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said: "We are bound by old family ties—but ritual has its constant honor.

sentences.zh: ”簡曰：“某守臣，使者銜天子命，辱臨敝邑，天使也，某不改不肅。

translations.literal: " Jian said: "I am a guarding minister; the envoy bears the Son of Heaven's command and deigns to come to this humble district—an imperial envoy; I cannot fail to be reverent.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian said: "I am a guarding minister; the envoy bears the Son of Heaven's command and deigns to visit this humble district—an imperial envoy; I cannot be less than reverent.

sentences.zh: ”遂從西翼偕進，禮北面東上，簡行則常西，步則後，及階，莫敢升，已乃同升自西階，足踧踧莫敢就主席，使者曰：“邦君之庭也，禮有常尊。

translations.literal: " They then advanced together from the western wing; in ritual they faced north and ascended east; when Jian walked he always kept to the west, and when he stepped he went behind; upon reaching the steps none dared ascend; afterward they ascended together from the western steps; feet faltered and none dared take the host's seat; the envoy said: "This is the lord of the state in his court; ritual has its constant honor.
translations.idiomatic: " They advanced together from the western wing; in ritual they faced north and ascended east; when Jian walked he kept to the west, and when he stepped he went behind; at the steps none dared ascend; then they ascended together from the western steps; feet faltered and none dared take the host's seat; the envoy said: "This is the lord of the state in his court; ritual has its constant honor.

sentences.zh: ”簡曰：“《春秋》，王人雖微，例書大國之上，尊天子也。

translations.literal: " Jian said: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, even when the king's envoy is lowly, the rule is to write him above a great state—to honor the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian said: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, even when the king's envoy is lowly, the rule writes him above a great state—to honor the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 況今天使乎？

translations.literal: How much more today an imperial envoy?
translations.idiomatic: How much more today an imperial envoy?

sentences.zh: ”持之益堅，使者辭益力，如是數刻，使者知不可變，乃曰：“某不敏，敢不敬承執事尊天子之義。

translations.literal: " He held to this all the more firmly; the envoy declined all the more forcefully; thus for several quarters; the envoy knew it could not be changed and then said: "I am dull; I dare not fail reverently to accept the minister's meaning of honoring the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " He held all the more firmly to this; the envoy declined all the more forcefully; thus for several quarters; the envoy saw it could not be changed and said: "I am dull; I dare not fail reverently to accept the minister's meaning of honoring the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: ”即揖而出。

translations.literal: " He then bowed and went out.
translations.idiomatic: " He then bowed and went out.

sentences.zh: 既就館，簡乃以賓禮見。

translations.literal: Once lodged at the guest house, Jian then received him with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Once lodged at the guest house, Jian received him with guest ritual.

sentences.zh: 儀典曠絕，邦人創見之，莫不瞿然竦觀，屏息立。

translations.literal: The ceremonial standards had long been lost; the people of the district saw it for the first time and all gazed in awe, holding their breath as they stood.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial standards had long been lost; the people of the district saw this for the first time and stood in awe, holding their breath.

sentences.zh: 簡在郡廉儉自將，奉養菲薄，常曰：“吾敢以赤子膏血自肥乎！

translations.literal: Jian in the prefecture was frugal and restrained himself; his support was thin, and he often said: "How dare I fatten myself on the blood and sweat of the people!
translations.idiomatic: Jian in the prefecture was frugal and restrained; his support was meager, and he often said: "How dare I fatten myself on the blood and sweat of the people!

sentences.zh: ”閭巷雍睦無忿爭聲，民愛之如父母，鹹畫象事之。

translations.literal: " In lanes and alleys harmony prevailed without sounds of angry quarrel; the people loved him as parents, and all painted his image to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: " In lanes and alleys harmony prevailed without angry quarrels; the people loved him as they love parents, and all painted his image to honor him.

sentences.zh: 遷駕部員外郎，老稚扶擁緣道，傾城哭送。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Outer Department Member; old and young supported one another along the road, and the whole city wept as they sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to outer department member; old and young supported one another along the road, and the whole city wept as they sent him off.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：“盡掃喜順惡逆之私情，善政盡舉，弊政盡除，民怨自銷，禍亂不作。

translations.literal: He entered for audience and said: "Sweep away private feelings of favoring the compliant and hating the contrary; good policies should all be raised, corrupt policies all removed—popular resentment will naturally dissolve and calamity and disorder will not arise.
translations.idiomatic: He entered for audience and said: "Sweep away private feelings that favor the compliant and hate the contrary; raise every good policy and remove every corrupt one—popular resentment will dissolve of itself, and calamity and disorder will not arise.

sentences.zh: ”改工部員外郎，轉對，又以擇賢久任為言。

translations.literal: " He was changed to Outer Department Member of the Ministry of Works; at the rotating audience he again spoke on selecting the worthy for long tenure.
translations.idiomatic: " He was changed to outer department member of the Ministry of Works; at the rotating audience he again spoke on selecting the worthy for long tenure.

sentences.zh: 遷軍器監兼工部郎官，轉朝奉大夫，又遷將作監兼國史院編修官兼實錄院檢討官，轉朝散大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Directorate of Armaments and concurrent Works Department Official, promoted to Grand Master for Court Audience, then transferred to Director of Palace Buildings and concurrent Compiler of the National History Office and Examiner of the Veritable Records Office, and promoted to Grand Master for Dispersed Duty.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Directorate of Armaments and concurrent works department official, promoted to grand master for court audience, then transferred to director of palace buildings and concurrent compiler of the National History Office and examiner of the Veritable Records Office, and promoted to grand master for dispersed duty.

sentences.zh: 金人大饑，來歸者日以數千、萬計。

translations.literal: The Jin people suffered great famine; those coming to surrender numbered several thousand or tens of thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin people suffered great famine; each day several thousand or tens of thousands came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 邊吏臨淮水射之。

translations.literal: Frontier officials shot them at the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials shot them at the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 簡戚然曰：“得土地易，得人心難。

translations.literal: Jian said sorrowfully: "Gaining territory is easy; gaining the people's hearts is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said sorrowfully: "Gaining territory is easy; winning hearts is hard.

sentences.zh: 薄海內外，皆吾赤子，中土故民，出塗炭，投慈父母，顧靳鬥升粟而迎殺之，蘄脫死乃速得死，豈相上帝綏四方之道哉？

translations.literal: Within and without the four seas, all are our infants; former subjects of the central land, escaping charcoal and fire, throw themselves upon a merciful parent—yet you begrudge a dou or sheng of grain and welcome them with killing; they sought to escape death yet quickly found death—how does this accord with the way of the August Lord pacifying the four quarters?
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the four seas, all are our children; former subjects of the central land, escaping fire and ash, throw themselves upon a merciful parent—yet you begrudge a dou or sheng of grain and greet them with death; they sought to escape death and found it swiftly—how does this accord with the August Lord's way of pacifying the four quarters?

sentences.zh: ”即日上奏，哀痛言之，不報。

translations.literal: " That same day he submitted a memorial, speaking of it in grief; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he submitted a memorial, speaking of it in grief; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 會有疾，請去益力，乃以直寶謨閣主管玉局觀。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he requested dismissal all the more forcefully; he was then made Direct Gentleman of the Baomo Pavilion and put in charge of Yuju Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he requested dismissal all the more forcefully; he was then made direct gentleman of the Baomo Pavilion and put in charge of Yuju Abbey.

sentences.zh: 升直寶文閣主管明道宮、秘閣修撰主管千秋鴻禧觀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Gentleman of the Baowen Pavilion, put in charge of Mingdao Palace, and Compiler of the Secret Archive in charge of Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct gentleman of the Baowen Pavilion, put in charge of Mingdao Palace, and compiler of the Secret Archive in charge of Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 特授朝請大夫、右文殿修撰主管鴻慶宮，賜紫衣金魚。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Gentleman for Court Service, Compiler of the Youwen Hall, and put in charge of Hongqing Palace, granted purple robes and gold fish.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed gentleman for court service, compiler of the Youwen Hall, and put in charge of Hongqing Palace, granted purple robes and gold fish.

sentences.zh: 進寶謨閣待制、提舉鴻慶宮，賜金帶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman-in-Waiting of the Baomo Pavilion and put in charge of Hongqing Palace, granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman-in-waiting of the Baomo Pavilion and put in charge of Hongqing Palace, granted a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，進寶謨閣直學士，賜金帶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Baomo Pavilion and granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong ascended the throne, he was promoted to direct academician of the Baomo Pavilion and granted a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年，轉朝議大夫、慈溪縣男，尋授華文閣直學士、提舉佑神觀，奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoqing he was transferred to Grand Master for Discussion and Baron of Cixi County; soon he was appointed Direct Academician of the Huawen Pavilion and put in charge of Youshen Abbey, attending court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoqing he was transferred to grand master for discussion and baron of Cixi County; soon he was appointed direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion and put in charge of Youshen Abbey, attending court.

sentences.zh: 詔入見，簡屢辭。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him for audience; Jian repeatedly declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him for audience; Jian repeatedly declined.

sentences.zh: 授敷文閣直學士，累加中大夫，仍提舉鴻慶宮，尋以寶謨閣學士、太中大夫致仕，卒，贈正奉大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion, repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Palace, still put in charge of Hongqing Palace; soon he retired as Academician of the Baomo Pavilion and Grand Master of the Palace; he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master for Proper Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct academician of the Fuwen Pavilion, repeatedly promoted to grand master of the palace, still put in charge of Hongqing Palace; soon he retired as academician of the Baomo Pavilion and grand master of the palace; he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as grand master for proper service.

sentences.zh: 簡所著有《甲稿》、《乙稿》、《冠記》、《昏記》《喪禮家記》、《家祭記》、《釋菜禮記》、《石魚家記》，又有《己易》、《啟蔽》等書，其論治務最急者五，其次八。

translations.literal: Jian's writings included Draft A, Draft B, Record of Capping, Record of Marriage, Family Record of Mourning Rites, Family Record of Sacrifices, Record of the Capping-and-Collating Rite, Record of the Stone Fish, and also books such as Self-Change and Opening Blindness; in governing he set forth five matters as most urgent and eight as next.
translations.idiomatic: Among Jian's writings were Draft A, Draft B, Record of Capping, Record of Marriage, Family Record of Mourning Rites, Family Record of Sacrifices, Record of the Capping-and-Collating Rite, Record of the Stone Fish, and also Self-Change, Opening Blindness, and other books; in governing he named five matters as most urgent and eight as next.

sentences.zh: 一曰謹擇左右大臣、近臣、小臣；

translations.literal: First, carefully select left and right chief ministers, close ministers, and minor ministers;
translations.idiomatic: First, carefully choose left and right chief ministers, close ministers, and minor ministers;

sentences.zh: 二曰擇賢以久任中外之官；

translations.literal: second, select the worthy for long tenure in offices within and without;
translations.idiomatic: second, choose the worthy and keep them long in office within and without;

sentences.zh: 三曰罷科舉而行鄉舉裏選；

translations.literal: third, abolish the civil service examination and implement local recommendation and selection;
translations.idiomatic: third, end the civil service examination and put local recommendation and selection in its place;

sentences.zh: 四曰罷設法道淫；

translations.literal: fourth, abolish the establishment of heterodox ways and licentiousness;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, abolish the establishment of heterodox ways and licentiousness;

sentences.zh: 五曰治伍法，修諸葛武侯之正兵，以備不虞。

translations.literal: fifth, rectify the company regulations and restore Zhuge Liang's orthodox troops to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, rectify company regulations and restore Zhuge Liang's orthodox troops to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 其次急者有八：一曰募兵屯田，以省養兵之費；

translations.literal: Among the next urgent matters there were eight: first, recruit soldiers for garrison farming to save the cost of maintaining troops;
translations.idiomatic: Among the next urgent matters were eight: first, recruit soldiers for garrison farming to reduce the cost of maintaining troops;

sentences.zh: 二曰限民田，以漸復井田；

translations.literal: second, limit private land to gradually restore the well-field system;
translations.idiomatic: second, cap private landholding to gradually restore the well-field system;

sentences.zh: 三曰罷妓籍，從良；

translations.literal: third, abolish the registry of courtesans and allow them to marry;
translations.idiomatic: third, abolish the registry of courtesans and permit them to marry;

sentences.zh: 四曰漸罷和買、折帛暨諸無名之賦及榷酤，而禁群飲；

translations.literal: fourth, gradually abolish government purchase, silk conversion, and all nameless levies and the salt and wine monopoly, and forbid group drinking;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, gradually abolish government purchase, silk conversion, all nameless levies, and the salt and wine monopoly, and forbid group drinking;

sentences.zh: 五曰擇賢士教之大學，教成，使分掌諸州之學，又使各擇井裏之士聚而教之，教成，使各分掌其邑裏之學；

translations.literal: fifth, select worthy scholars to teach them at the Imperial Academy; when teaching is complete, have them each manage the schools of the various prefectures, and also have each select scholars of the lanes and hamlets to gather and teach them; when teaching is complete, have each manage the schools of their districts;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, choose worthy scholars to teach at the Imperial Academy; when their teaching is complete, have them manage the schools of the various prefectures, and also have each choose scholars of the lanes and hamlets to gather and teach; when that teaching is complete, have each manage the schools of their district;

sentences.zh: 六曰取《周禮》及古書，會議熟講其可行於今者行之；

translations.literal: sixth, take the Rites of Zhou and ancient books, convene discussion, thoroughly examine what can be implemented today, and implement it;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, take the Rites of Zhou and ancient books, convene discussion, thoroughly examine what can be put into practice today, and put it into practice;

sentences.zh: 七曰禁淫樂；

translations.literal: seventh, forbid licentious music;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, forbid licentious music;

sentences.zh: 八曰修書以削邪說。

translations.literal: eighth, compile books to cut down heterodox doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: eighth, compile books to suppress heterodox doctrines.

sentences.zh: 此簡之誌也。

translations.literal: This was Jian's purpose.
translations.idiomatic: This was Jian's purpose.

sentences.zh: 後鹹淳間，製置使劉黻即其居作慈湖書院。

translations.literal: Later in the Chunyou era, Pacification Commissioner Liu Fu built Cihu Academy at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later in the Chunyou era, pacification commissioner Liu Fu built Cihu Academy at his residence.

sentences.zh: 門人錢時。

translations.literal: His disciple was Qian Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple was Qian Shi.

sentences.zh: 時字子是，淳安人。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Zishi, was a man of Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, whose courtesy name was Zishi, came from Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 幼奇偉不群，讀書不為世儒之習。

translations.literal: In youth he was singularly lofty and stood apart from the crowd; in reading he did not follow the habits of worldly Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was singularly lofty and stood apart; in reading he did not follow the habits of worldly Confucians.

sentences.zh: 以《易》冠漕司，既而絕意科舉，究明理學。

translations.literal: He took first place in the transport commission examination in the Classic of Changes, then abandoned the civil service examination and thoroughly investigated Neo-Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the transport commission examination in the Classic of Changes, then abandoned the civil service examination and pursued Neo-Confucian learning to its depths.

sentences.zh: 江東提刑袁甫作象山書院，招主講席，學者興起，政事多所裨益。

translations.literal: Jiangdong Surveillance Commissioner Yuan Fu established Xiangshan Academy and invited him to head the lecture seat; scholars flourished and many affairs of government were helped.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdong surveillance commissioner Yuan Fu established Xiangshan Academy and invited him to head the lecture seat; scholars flourished and many affairs of government were helped.

sentences.zh: 郡守及新安、紹興守皆厚禮延請，開講郡庠。

translations.literal: The prefect and the magistrates of Xin'an and Shaoxing all treated him with thick courtesy and extended invitations, opening lectures at the prefectural schools.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect and the magistrates of Xin'an and Shaoxing all treated him with great courtesy and invited him to open lectures at the prefectural schools.

sentences.zh: 其學大抵發明人心，論議宏偉，指擿痛決，聞者皆有得焉。

translations.literal: His learning mostly elucidated the human mind; his discourse was grand and his pointing out was sharp and decisive; those who heard all gained something.
translations.idiomatic: His learning mostly elucidated the human mind; his discourse was grand, his judgments sharp and decisive; all who heard gained something.

sentences.zh: 丞相喬行簡知其賢，特薦之朝，且曰：“時夙負才識，尤通世務，田裏之休戚利病，當世之是非得失，莫不詳究而熟知之，不但通詩書、守陳言而已。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Qiao Xingjian knew his worth and specially recommended him to the court, saying: "Shi has long possessed talent and insight and is especially versed in worldly affairs; the joys and sorrows, benefits and harms of fields and hamlets, and the rights and wrongs and gains and losses of the age—none are not thoroughly investigated and well known; he is not merely one who knows poetry and books and keeps to old formulas.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councillor Qiao Xingjian knew his worth and specially recommended him to the court, saying: "Shi has long possessed talent and insight and is especially versed in worldly affairs; the joys and sorrows, benefits and harms of fields and hamlets, and the rights and wrongs and gains and losses of the age—none are not thoroughly investigated and well known; he is not merely one who knows poetry and books and keeps to old formulas.

sentences.zh: 授秘閣校勘。

translations.literal: He was appointed Collator of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed collator of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 詔守臣以時所著書來上。

translations.literal: An edict ordered guarding ministers to submit the books Shi had written.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered guarding ministers to submit the books Shi had written at the proper time.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出佐浙東倉幕，太史李心傳奏召史館檢閱。

translations.literal: Before long he went out to serve on the staff of the eastern Zhejiang granary office; Grand Astrologer Li Xinchuan memorialized to summon him as examiner in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went out to serve on the staff of the eastern Zhejiang granary office; grand astrologer Li Xinchuan memorialized to summon him as examiner in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 轉對，敷陳剴切，皆聖賢之精微。

translations.literal: At the rotating audience he set forth incisive and earnest views, all the subtle essentials of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: At the rotating audience he set forth incisive and earnest views—all the subtle essentials of the sages.

sentences.zh: 旋以國史宏綱未畢求去，授江東帥屬，歸。

translations.literal: Soon, because the great outline of the national history was not finished he requested leave; he was appointed staff officer to the Jiangdong commander and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because the great outline of the national history was unfinished, he requested leave; he was appointed staff officer to the Jiangdong commander and returned home.

sentences.zh: 其書有《周易釋傳》、《尚書演義》《學詩管見》、《春秋大旨》、《四書管見》、《兩漢筆記》、《蜀阜集》、《冠昏記》、《百行冠冕集》。

translations.literal: His books included Exegesis of the Changes, Exposition of the Documents, Overview of Learning the Odes, Great Purport of the Spring and Autumn, Overview of the Four Books, Notes on the Two Han Dynasties, Collection from Shufu, Record of Capping and Marriage, and Collection of the Crown of the Hundred Conducts.
translations.idiomatic: Among his books were Exegesis of the Changes, Exposition of the Documents, Overview of Learning the Odes, Great Purport of the Spring and Autumn, Overview of the Four Books, Notes on the Two Han Dynasties, Collection from Shufu, Record of Capping and Marriage, and Collection of the Crown of the Hundred Conducts.

sentences.zh: 寶祐間，守季鏞祠於學。

translations.literal: In the Bao you era, Magistrate Ji Yong enshrined him in the school.
translations.idiomatic: In the Bao you era, magistrate Ji Yong enshrined him in the school.

sentences.zh: 張虙，字子宓，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu, styled Zimi, was a man of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu, whose courtesy name was Zimi, came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingyuan he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 故事，潛邸進士升名，虙不以自陳。

translations.literal: By precedent, jinshi from the hidden residence were promoted in rank; Fu did not claim this for himself.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, jinshi from the hidden residence were promoted in rank; Fu did not claim the promotion for himself.

sentences.zh: 授州教授。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefectural instructor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefectural instructor.

sentences.zh: 為浙東帥屬。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer to the eastern Zhejiang commander.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer to the eastern Zhejiang commander.

sentences.zh: 帥督新昌舊逋，虙手書諫曰：“越人之瘠，宜咻噢撫摩之。

translations.literal: The commander pressed collection of old arrears in Xinchang; Fu wrote a remonstrance by hand saying: "The emaciation of the Yue people should be soothed and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: The commander pressed collection of old arrears in Xinchang; Fu wrote a remonstrance by hand: "The emaciation of the Yue people calls for soothing and comfort.

sentences.zh: 今夏稅當寬為之期，使田裏久饑之，少還已耗之氣血，尚可理舊逋耶？

translations.literal: This year's summer tax should be given a broad extension; let the fields and hamlets, long famished, restore a little of their depleted vitality—can old arrears still be settled?
translations.idiomatic: This year's summer tax ought to be given a broad extension; let the fields and hamlets, long famished, recover a little of their depleted strength—can old arrears still be collected?

sentences.zh: ”力辭不行。

translations.literal: " He forcefully declined and would not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: " He forcefully declined and would not carry it out.

sentences.zh: 主管戶部架閣文字，改太學正。

translations.literal: He was put in charge of archival documents in the Ministry of Revenue and changed to Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of archival documents in the Ministry of Revenue and changed to director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時新進者多逞小才、害大體，轉對言：“立國有大經，人主當以靜製天下之動。

translations.literal: At the time many newly advanced men displayed petty talent and harmed the larger structure; at the rotating audience he said: "Establishing a state has a great constant; the ruler should use stillness to control the realm's motion.
translations.idiomatic: Many newly advanced men at the time displayed petty talent and harmed the larger structure; at the rotating audience he said: "Establishing a state has a great constant; the ruler should use stillness to govern the realm's motion.

sentences.zh: 今日之治，或有鄰於鍥薄，而咈人心、傷國體者，宜有以革之，使祖宗之意常如一日可也。

translations.literal: In today's governance, some things approach the thin and shallow and offend the human heart and harm the body of the state—there should be means to reform them, so that the intent of the ancestors may remain as on a single day.
translations.idiomatic: In today's governance some things approach the thin and shallow, offend the human heart, and harm the body of the state—there should be means to reform them, so that the ancestors' intent may endure as on a single day.

sentences.zh: ”帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，又遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred to Doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred to doctor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 時金垂亡，因論自治之道，謂：“天下之治，必有根本。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin was near extinction; he therefore discussed the way of self-governance, saying: "Governing the realm must have a root foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin was near extinction; he therefore discussed the way of self-governance, saying: "To govern the realm one must have a root foundation.

sentences.zh: 城郭所以禦敵也，使溝壑有轉徙之民，則何敵之能禦？

translations.literal: City walls are for repelling the enemy—if ditches and gullies have displaced people wandering, then what enemy can be repelled?
translations.idiomatic: City walls exist to repel the enemy—if ditches and gullies are filled with displaced wanderers, what enemy can be repelled?

sentences.zh: 儲峙所以備患也，使枵腹盻盻不得食，則何患之能備？

translations.literal: Stored grain is for guarding against calamity—if hollow-bellied people gaze longingly yet cannot obtain food, then what calamity can be guarded against?
translations.idiomatic: Stored grain exists to guard against calamity—if hollow-bellied people gaze longingly yet cannot eat, what calamity can be guarded against?

sentences.zh: 今日之吏，能知守邊之務者多，而能明立國之意者少。

translations.literal: Today's officials mostly know the tasks of guarding the frontier, yet few clearly understand the intent of establishing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Today's officials mostly know the tasks of guarding the frontier, yet few clearly grasp the intent of establishing the state.

sentences.zh: 繕城郭，聚米粟，恃此而不恤乎民，則其策下矣。

translations.literal: Repairing walls and gathering grain, relying on these yet not caring for the people—that policy is low indeed.
translations.idiomatic: To repair walls and gather grain, relying on these yet not caring for the people—that is a low policy indeed.

sentences.zh: 時以旱求言，即上疏曰：“上天之心即我祖宗之心，數年以來，蓋有為祖宗所不敢為者。

translations.literal: When drought led the court to seek advice, he immediately submitted a memorial saying: "The heart of Heaven is the heart of our ancestors; in recent years there have surely been things our ancestors would not have dared to do.
translations.idiomatic: When drought led the court to seek advice, he immediately submitted a memorial: "The heart of Heaven is the heart of our ancestors; in recent years there have surely been things our ancestors would not have dared to do.

sentences.zh: 凡祖宗之時，幾舉而不遂，已行而復寢，始以人言而從，終以國體而回者，今皆處之以不疑矣。

translations.literal: Whatever in the time of the ancestors was several times proposed yet not carried through, already implemented yet again suspended, first followed because of human speech yet in the end turned back because of the body of the state—today all are treated without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever in the ancestors' time was proposed several times yet not carried through, implemented yet suspended again, first followed because of human speech yet in the end turned back for the sake of the state—today all are treated without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 凡祖宗長慮卻顧，所以銷惡運、遏亂原、兢兢相與守之者，皆變於目前利便快意之謀矣。

translations.literal: Whatever the ancestors long considered and held back from, by which they extinguished evil trends and checked the sources of disorder and carefully guarded together—today all have changed into schemes for immediate convenience and quick satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the ancestors long considered and held back from, by which they extinguished evil trends, checked the sources of disorder, and carefully guarded together—today all have become schemes for immediate convenience and quick satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 議者惟知衰靡之俗不可不振起也，圮壞之風不可不整刷也，抑不知振起整刷之術，最難施於衰靡圮壞之後。

translations.literal: Counselors know only that decadent customs cannot fail to be roused and ruined winds cannot fail to be swept clean, yet they do not know that the art of rousing and sweeping clean is hardest to apply after decadence and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors know only that decadent customs must be roused and ruined winds swept clean, yet they do not know that the art of rousing and sweeping clean is hardest to apply after decadence and ruin.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 元氣已傷而不可再擾，人心方蘇而不可駭動也。

translations.literal: The vital energy is already injured and cannot again be disturbed; the human heart has just revived and cannot again be startled into motion.
translations.idiomatic: The vital energy is already injured and cannot be disturbed again; the human heart has just revived and cannot be startled into motion again.

sentences.zh: 且造楮初欲便民，朝廷既以一切之政駴其聽，復以一定之價迫之從，郡縣之間，遂騷然矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, when paper currency was first created the intent was to benefit the people; the court first used catch-all policies to startle their hearing, then used fixed prices to force compliance; between prefectures and districts thereupon arose turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When paper currency was first created the intent was to benefit the people; the court first used catch-all policies to startle them, then fixed prices to force compliance—and between prefectures and districts turmoil arose.

sentences.zh: 監司、郡守老成遲鈍者悉屏而不用，而取夫新進喜功名者為之，見事則風生，臨事則痛決，事未果集而根本已朘，國未有益而民生已困矣。

translations.literal: Surveillance commissioners and prefects who were old, mature, and slow were all removed and not used, and instead those newly advanced who delighted in fame and achievement were taken; when they saw affairs they acted like wind, and when facing affairs they decided with severity; before affairs were gathered and settled the root was already depleted—the state had not yet benefited yet the people's livelihood was already distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioners and prefects who were old, mature, and deliberate were all removed; in their place were taken men newly advanced who delighted in fame and achievement; when they saw affairs they acted like wind, and when facing affairs they decided with severity; before affairs were settled the root was already depleted—the state had not yet benefited, yet the people's livelihood was already in distress.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆有累於祖宗仁厚之德，此旱勢之所以彌甚也。

translations.literal: All of these have been burdens on the benevolent and generous virtue of the ancestors; this is why the drought has grown all the more severe.
translations.idiomatic: All of this has weighed upon the benevolent and generous virtue of the ancestors; this is why the drought has grown all the more severe.

sentences.zh: 遷國子監丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 轉對，願力主正論，勿使迎合之人得以投吾機。

translations.literal: At the rotating audience he wished to uphold orthodox discourse firmly and not let flatterers be able to seize our openings.
translations.idiomatic: At the rotating audience he wished firmly to uphold orthodox discourse and not let flatterers seize our openings.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書郎，預編《寧宗會要》兼吳、益王府教授，改兼莊文府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary Gentleman, participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Ningzong and concurrently served as instructor to the Wu and Yi princely establishments, then changed to the Zhuangwen princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary gentleman, participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Ningzong and concurrently served as instructor to the Wu and Yi princely establishments, then changed to the Zhuangwen princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 講《毛詩》終篇，乞以所讀諸子改讀《尚書》，帝曰：“吾固以《詩》、《書》成麟趾之美也。

translations.literal: Having lectured through the Mao Odes, he requested to change from the various masters he had read to reading the Documents; the emperor said: "I have always intended that the Odes and Documents should complete the beauty of linzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Having lectured through the Mao Odes, he asked to change from the various masters he had read to the Documents; the emperor said: "I have always intended that the Odes and Documents should complete the beauty of linzhi.

sentences.zh: 遷著作佐郎兼權都官郎官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Compiler and concurrent Acting Punishments Department Official.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant compiler and concurrent acting punishments department official.

sentences.zh: 轉對言：“邊事有二病，戒敕千條，猶患悖繆，指意明白，猶復背違，安有不示其所向而謂可責其成。

translations.literal: At the rotating audience he said: "Frontier affairs have two illnesses: though admonitions number a thousand, one still fears perversity; though intent is clear, there is still violation—how can success be demanded without showing where one is headed?
translations.idiomatic: At the rotating audience he said: "Frontier affairs have two illnesses: though admonitions number a thousand, perversity is still feared; though intent is clear, violation still occurs—how can success be demanded without showing where one is headed?

sentences.zh: 且言戰則當知彼，言和則當請於彼，惟守則自求諸己而已。

translations.literal: When speaking of war one must know the enemy; when speaking of peace one must request it from the enemy; only in defense does one seek it in oneself.
translations.idiomatic: In speaking of war one must know the enemy; in speaking of peace one must request it from the enemy; only in defense does one seek the answer in oneself.

sentences.zh: 儻以為可，則當力主其說，明告天下，日講求其所以守之之策，蓋議論貴合一，而今則病乎雜也。

translations.literal: If it is thought feasible, then one should forcefully uphold that doctrine, clearly inform the realm, and daily seek the policies by which to defend—the value of counsel lies in unity, yet today the illness is confusion.
translations.idiomatic: If it is thought feasible, then one should forcefully uphold that doctrine, clearly inform the realm, and daily seek policies of defense—the value of counsel lies in unity, yet today the illness is confusion.

sentences.zh: 用人不可以嚐試，任人不可以自疑。

translations.literal: In employing men one cannot use trial and error; in entrusting men one cannot harbor self-doubt.
translations.idiomatic: In employing men one cannot experiment by trial; in entrusting men one cannot harbor self-doubt.

sentences.zh: 朝廷惟慮獨任之難勝，彼此互分，不相扶持，人得抗衡，莫有稟屬，製置但存虛器，便宜反出多門。

translations.literal: The court only fears that sole responsibility is hard to bear; each side divides duties and does not support one another; men can resist one another and none receives orders; the pacification commissioner retains only an empty title, while discretionary authority in fact issues from many gates.
translations.idiomatic: The court fears only that sole responsibility is hard to bear; each side divides duties and does not support the other; men can resist one another and none receives orders; the pacification commissioner keeps only an empty title, while discretionary authority in fact issues from many gates.

sentences.zh: 蓋體貴合一，而今則病乎分也。

translations.literal: The body of policy values unity, yet today the illness is division.
translations.idiomatic: Policy as a whole values unity—yet today the illness is division.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞，改著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary Assistant Director and changed to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary assistant director and changed to compiler.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞外，出知南康。

translations.literal: Because of illness he requested an outside post and went out as prefect of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to request an outside post; he went out as prefect of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 至郡，剖決滯訟，眾皆悅服。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture he decided stalled lawsuits; the multitude all submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the prefecture he decided stalled lawsuits, and the multitude submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 前守陳宓以錢七千緡置濟民庫為築城費，虙至，曰：“不必取贏於民，吾捐萬緡為倡，繼是倘不已，何患事之難成。

translations.literal: The former prefect Chen Mi had set aside seven thousand strings of cash in the Relief-for-the-People Office as funds for building the wall; when Fu arrived he said: "There is no need to take surplus from the people; I donate ten thousand strings as a beginning—if others follow without ceasing, why worry that the task will be hard to complete?
translations.idiomatic: The former prefect Chen Mi had set aside seven thousand strings of cash in the Relief-for-the-People Office for building the wall; when Fu arrived he said: "There is no need to squeeze surplus from the people; I will donate ten thousand strings to begin—if others follow without ceasing, why fear the task will be hard to finish?

sentences.zh: ”轉運使以錢萬二千緡置平糴於郡，虙復出錢萬二千緡以增益之，民賴其利。

translations.literal: " The transport commissioner set aside twelve thousand strings for equitable grain purchase in the prefecture; Fu again contributed twelve thousand strings to increase it, and the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: " The transport commissioner set aside twelve thousand strings for equitable grain purchase in the prefecture; Fu added another twelve thousand strings, and the people benefited.

sentences.zh: 將增建禁旅，營地屬民者，索質劑視元直償之。

translations.literal: When the forbidden guard was to be expanded, for camp land belonging to commoners he sought deeds and compensated them at the original price.
translations.idiomatic: When the forbidden guard was to be expanded, for camp land belonging to commoners he sought deeds and paid compensation at the original price.

sentences.zh: 徙知處州，移知溫州，力辭，遂直秘閣、主管千秋鴻禧觀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Chuzhou, then moved to prefect of Wenzhou; he forcefully declined and then served as Direct Gentleman of the Secret Archive and put in charge of Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Chuzhou, then moved to prefect of Wenzhou; he forcefully declined and then served as direct gentleman of the Secret Archive and put in charge of Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 參議製置使幕中，使者尚威力，愎諫自用，虙守正不阿，每濟以寬大。

translations.literal: As deliberator in the Pacification Commissioner's staff, the envoy valued power and severity, was obstinate in remonstrance and self-willed; Fu upheld rectitude without yielding and always tempered matters with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: As deliberator in the pacification commissioner's staff, the envoy valued power and severity, was obstinate in remonstrance and self-willed; Fu upheld rectitude without yielding and always tempered matters with leniency.

sentences.zh: 又上書論海防利便。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial discussing the benefits and conveniences of coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted a memorial on the benefits and conveniences of coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 主管玉局觀。

translations.literal: He was put in charge of Yuju Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of Yuju Abbey.

sentences.zh: 端平初，召為國子司業兼侍講，以《禮記月令》進讀，至“獄訟必端平”之語，因敷暢厥旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping he was summoned as Vice Director of the National University and Lecturer-in-Waiting; he advanced reading of the Monthly Ordinances of the Book of Rites, and when he reached the phrase "litigation must be even and fair" he expounded its purport.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duanping he was summoned as vice director of the National University and lecturer-in-waiting; he advanced reading of the Monthly Ordinances of the Book of Rites, and when he reached the phrase "litigation must be even and fair" he expounded its purport.

sentences.zh: 八陵來復，將議修奉，而論者未能協一，虙議曰：“當乘此時遣官肅清威儀，申祗奉故事，如或為其所紿，功未即就，亦足以感動天下忠臣義士之心。

translations.literal: When the eight imperial tombs were recovered, repair and maintenance were to be discussed, yet counselors could not agree; Fu argued: "At this time officials should be dispatched to solemnly restore ceremonial dignity and reverently carry out the old observances; even if one is deceived by the enemy and the work is not immediately accomplished, it is still enough to move the hearts of loyal ministers and righteous men throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the eight imperial tombs were recovered, repair and maintenance were to be discussed, yet counselors could not agree; Fu argued: "At this time officials should be dispatched to solemnly restore ceremonial dignity and reverently carry out the old observances; even if the enemy deceives us and the work is not immediately accomplished, it is still enough to move the hearts of loyal ministers and righteous men throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: ”力辭勸講之職，升國子祭酒。

translations.literal: " He forcefully declined the lecturing post and was promoted to Libationer of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: " He forcefully declined the lecturing post and was promoted to libationer of the National University.

sentences.zh: 以為“《月令》之書雖出於呂不韋，然人主後天而奉天時，此書不為無助”。

translations.literal: He held that "though the book of the Monthly Ordinances comes from Lü Buwei, yet the ruler follows Heaven after Heaven and observes the seasons—this book is not without help."
translations.idiomatic: He held that "though the book of the Monthly Ordinances comes from Lü Buwei, the ruler follows Heaven after Heaven and observes the seasons—this book is not without use."

sentences.zh: 乃因已講者為十二卷，乞按月而觀之。

translations.literal: He then took what he had already lectured and made twelve juan, requesting that it be viewed month by month.
translations.idiomatic: He then compiled what he had already lectured into twelve juan and asked that it be viewed month by month.

sentences.zh: 兼權工部侍郎兼國子祭酒，命下而卒，詔贈四官。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Acting Vice Minister of Works and Libationer of the National University; the order was issued and he died; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as acting vice minister of works and libationer of the National University; the order was issued and he died; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him four ranks.

sentences.zh: 呂午，字伯可，歙縣人。

translations.literal: Lu Wu, styled Boke, was a man of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wu, whose courtesy name was Boke, came from She County.

sentences.zh: 嘉定四年進士，授烏程主簿，郡守致之幕下，事一決於午。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed chief clerk of Wucheng, and the prefect brought him into his staff; all affairs were decided by Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed chief clerk of Wucheng, and the prefect brought him onto his staff; all affairs were decided by Wu.

sentences.zh: 守張忠恕，丞相浚之孫，薦午猶力，時忠恕之母就養，而時時躬至簿聽迎午二親入郡，與午皆衣彩衣奉觴上壽，邦人榮之。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Zhongshu, grandson of Chief Councillor Jun, recommended Wu with special force; at the time Zhongshu's mother was receiving support in the prefecture, and he himself often came in person to the clerk's hall to welcome Wu's two parents into the prefecture; Wu and Zhongshu all wore colored robes and offered cups to toast long life—the people of the district honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Zhongshu, grandson of chief councillor Jun, recommended Wu with special force; at the time Zhongshu's mother was receiving support in the prefecture, and he himself often came in person to the clerk's hall to welcome Wu's two parents into the prefecture; Wu and Zhongshu all wore colored robes and offered cups to toast long life—the people of the district honored this.

sentences.zh: 調當塗縣丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Dangtu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Dangtu County.

sentences.zh: 守吳柔勝謂午有操守，俾其子淵、潛定交焉。

translations.literal: Prefect Wu Rousheng said Wu had integrity in conduct and had his sons Yuan and Qian fix friendship with him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wu Rousheng said Wu had integrity in conduct and had his sons Yuan and Qian establish friendship with him.

sentences.zh: 會司理攝蕪湖縣，廬州遣兩兵會公事，司理遂以廬兵奪縣民為言。

translations.literal: When the judicial officer was acting as magistrate of Wuhu County, Luzhou sent two soldiers on official business; the judicial officer then spoke of Luzhou soldiers seizing county commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When the judicial officer was acting magistrate of Wuhu County, Luzhou sent two soldiers on official business; the judicial officer then spoke of Luzhou soldiers seizing county commoners.

sentences.zh: 柔勝怒，悉置獄，屬午問之。

translations.literal: Rousheng was angry and put them all in prison, assigning the matter to Wu for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Rousheng was angry and imprisoned them all, assigning the inquiry to Wu.

sentences.zh: 午謂“ 廬州有公櫝，不可謂奪民”。

translations.literal: Wu said: "Luzhou has an official chest—this cannot be called seizing commoners."
translations.idiomatic: Wu replied: "Luzhou maintains an official chest—this cannot be styled seizing commoners."

sentences.zh: 柔勝愈怒，再以屬午。

translations.literal: Rousheng grew angrier and again assigned it to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Rousheng grew angrier and again assigned the matter to Wu.

sentences.zh: 明日，午入謁，柔勝先令左右問若何，午執前說。

translations.literal: The next day Wu entered to pay respects; Rousheng first had attendants ask how it stood; Wu held to his previous view.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wu entered to pay respects; Rousheng first had attendants ask how it stood; Wu held to his earlier view.

sentences.zh: 柔勝益加怒，謂“我不忍廬兵奪吾百姓”。

translations.literal: Rousheng grew even angrier and said: "I cannot bear Luzhou soldiers seizing my commoners."
translations.idiomatic: Rousheng grew angrier still and declared: "I will not tolerate Luzhou soldiers seizing my commoners."

sentences.zh: 不出迎午，午坐客位不退，不食。

translations.literal: He did not come out to welcome Wu; Wu sat in the guest seat and did not withdraw, and did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: He did not come out to welcome Wu; Wu sat in the guest seat and would not withdraw, and would not eat.

sentences.zh: 柔勝勉為出，怒不息，欲黥二兵。

translations.literal: Rousheng reluctantly came out; his anger did not cease, and he wished to tattoo the two soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Rousheng came out with reluctance; his anger did not abate, and he meant to tattoo the two soldiers.

sentences.zh: 午徐曰：“廬州初無公櫝則可，有則縣不為處置而反罪廬兵，恐不可。

translations.literal: Wu said slowly: "If Luzhou originally had no official chest that would be one thing; since there is one, for the county not to dispose of the matter yet instead punish Luzhou soldiers— I fear this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Wu said slowly: "If Luzhou originally had no official chest, that would be one thing; since there is one, for the county not to dispose of the matter yet punish Luzhou soldiers—I fear this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: ”久之，卒從午請，由是柔勝益知午。

translations.literal: " After a long time Rousheng at last followed Wu's request; from this Rousheng came to know Wu better.
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while Rousheng at last followed Wu's request; from this he came to know Wu better.

sentences.zh: 陳貴誼守太平，屬午安集淮南流民。

translations.literal: When Chen Guiyi was prefect of Taiping, he assigned Wu to settle displaced people south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Guiyi served as prefect of Taiping, he charged Wu with settling displaced people south of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 江東提舉徐僑知午在郡，驚喜，辟為幕屬。

translations.literal: Jiangdong Intendant Xu Qiao, knowing Wu was in the prefecture, was delighted and invited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdong intendant Xu Qiao, knowing Wu was in the prefecture, was delighted and invited him as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 午欲盡決遣郡事而後行，帖趣行至十八而不以白貴誼，僑貽書貴誼，午始行。

translations.literal: Wu wished to decide all prefectural affairs before departing; urgent notices arrived eighteen times yet he did not inform Guiyi; Qiao sent a letter to Guiyi, and Wu then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu wished to decide all prefectural affairs before departing; eighteen urgent notices arrived, yet he did not inform Guiyi; Qiao sent a letter to Guiyi, and Wu then departed.

sentences.zh: 既而僑行部，以田事迕丞相史彌遠，以言罷。

translations.literal: Soon Qiao toured his jurisdiction; because of a land affair he offended Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan and was dismissed because of a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qiao toured his jurisdiction; because of a land affair he offended chief councillor Shi Miyuan and was dismissed because of a memorial.

sentences.zh: 午還當塗。

translations.literal: Wu returned to Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu returned to Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 監溫州天富北監鹽場，改知餘杭縣，亦以言罷，公論大不平，然午自此名益重。

translations.literal: He supervised the Tianfu North Salt Station in Wenzhou, then was changed to magistrate of Yuhang County; he too was dismissed because of a memorial; public opinion was greatly indignant, yet from this Wu's reputation grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Tianfu North Salt Station in Wenzhou, then was changed to magistrate of Yuhang County; he too was dismissed because of a memorial; public opinion was greatly indignant, yet from this Wu's reputation grew all the heavier.

sentences.zh: 浙東提舉章良朋留之幕，旋兼沿海製置司事。

translations.literal: Eastern Zhejiang Intendant Zhang Liangpeng kept him on his staff and soon had him concurrently handle affairs of the Coastal Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhejiang intendant Zhang Liangpeng kept him on his staff and soon had him concurrently handle affairs of the Coastal Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 海寇未平，良朋問策安在。

translations.literal: Sea bandits were not yet pacified; Liangpeng asked where the strategy lay.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandits had not yet been pacified; Liangpeng asked where the strategy was.

sentences.zh: 午廉知調軍出海，糧盡即還，軍獲寇物，官盡拘收，乃與製置司幹官施一飛議，糧盡再給，不許擅還，賊舟所有，悉以給軍，海道遂清。

translations.literal: Wu secretly learned that when troops were mobilized to go to sea, once grain was exhausted they returned; when the army captured bandit goods, the government confiscated them all; he then discussed with Pacification Commission staff officer Shi Yifei: when grain was exhausted, supply again; unauthorized return was not permitted; everything on bandit boats was given to the army, and the sea routes were then cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Wu secretly learned that when troops were mobilized to go to sea, once grain was exhausted they returned; when the army captured bandit goods, the government confiscated them all; he then discussed with pacification commission staff officer Shi Yifei: when grain was exhausted, supply again; unauthorized return was not permitted; everything on bandit boats was given to the army, and the sea routes were then cleared.

sentences.zh: 差知龍陽縣。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Longyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as magistrate of Longyang County.

sentences.zh: 豪民陶守忠殺人，正其獄誅之。

translations.literal: Powerful commoner Tao Shouzhong committed murder; Wu corrected the case and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful commoner Tao Shouzhong committed murder; Wu corrected the case and executed him.

sentences.zh: 彌遠雖非賢相，猶置人才簿，書賢士大夫以待用，而午治縣之政亦書之。

translations.literal: Though Miyuan was not a worthy chief councillor, he still kept a talent register, writing worthy scholar-officials to await employment—and Wu's governance as magistrate was also entered in it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Miyuan was not a worthy chief councillor, he still kept a talent register, writing worthy scholar-officials to await employment—and Wu's governance as magistrate was entered in it as well.

sentences.zh: 差兩浙轉運司主管文字，彌遠病久不見客，午入謁，特出迎。

translations.literal: Assigned as chief clerk of the two-Zhejiang Transport Commission, Miyuan had long been ill and did not see visitors; when Wu entered to pay respects, he specially came out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as chief clerk of the two-Zhejiang Transport Commission, Miyuan had long been ill and saw no visitors; when Wu entered to pay respects, he specially came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 運使罷，故不用人，以午護印半年。

translations.literal: When the transport commissioner was dismissed, since no replacement was used, Wu guarded the seal for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: When the transport commissioner was dismissed and no replacement appointed, Wu guarded the seal for half a year.

sentences.zh: 或問彌遠，何以不注官？

translations.literal: Someone asked Miyuan why he did not appoint an official.
translations.idiomatic: Someone questioned Miyuan as to why he had not appointed an official.

sentences.zh: 彌遠曰：“爾謂護印官不能耶？

translations.literal: Miyuan said: "Do you think the seal-guarding official cannot do it?
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan said: "Do you think the man guarding the seal cannot do the work?

sentences.zh: ”午聞之力辭。

translations.literal: " When Wu heard this he forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wu heard this he forcefully declined.

sentences.zh: 差監三省樞密院門兼監提轄封樁上庫。

translations.literal: He was assigned to supervise the gate of the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently supervise the Seal and Store Upper Warehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to supervise the gate of the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs, and concurrently to supervise the Seal and Store Upper Warehouse.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，免喪，遷大府寺簿。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he mourned; when mourning ended he was transferred to secretary of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father's death; when mourning ended he was transferred to secretary of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，帝親擢也。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor—the emperor personally selected him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor—the emperor personally selected him.

sentences.zh: 鄭清之喪師，至是丁黼死於成都，史嵩之、孟珙在京湖，嵩之尋升督府。

translations.literal: Zheng Qingzhi lost the army; by then Ding Fu had died at Chengdu; Shi Songzhi and Meng Gong were in Jinghu; Songzhi soon rose to command the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qingzhi had lost the army; by then Ding Fu had died at Chengdu; Shi Songzhi and Meng Gong were in Jinghu; Songzhi soon rose to command the commission.

sentences.zh: 陳韡、杜杲在淮西，王鑒在黃州，計用兵十七萬人，圍始解。

translations.literal: Chen Kai and Du Gao were in western Huai; Wang Jian was at Huangzhou; it was calculated that 170,000 troops were used before the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kai and Du Gao were in western Huai; Wang Jian was at Huangzhou; it took 170,000 troops before the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 獨趙葵在淮東不受兵，而坐視不出兵應援。

translations.literal: Only Zhao Kui in eastern Huai did not receive troops, yet sat watching and did not send troops to support.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhao Kui in eastern Huai received no troops, yet sat watching and sent none to support.

sentences.zh: 午疏論：“邊閫角立，當協心釋嫌，而乃幸災樂禍，無同舟共濟之心。

translations.literal: Wu submitted a memorial arguing: "Frontier commanders stand like horns; they should join hearts and release suspicion, yet instead they rejoice in others' disasters—there is no heart of sharing one boat and crossing together.
