translations.idiomatic: Wu memorialized: "Frontier commanders stand like horns—they should join hearts and release suspicion, yet they rejoice in others' disasters; there is no heart of sharing one boat and crossing together.

sentences.zh: ”葵以為午黨京湖製司，而嵩之亦憾午，乃遷宗正少卿兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: " Kui thought Wu sided with the Jinghu Pacification Commission, and Songzhi also resented Wu; he was then transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and concurrent Compiler of the National History Office and Examiner of the Veritable Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: " Kui thought Wu sided with the Jinghu Pacification Commission, and Songzhi also resented Wu; he was then transferred to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and concurrent compiler of the National History Office and examiner of the Veritable Records Office.

sentences.zh: 出知泉州。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，左丞相李宗勉深以葵之言為疑，會來自淮東者，乃言台官皆以葵交書，獨呂御史無之，宗勉始以午為賢，語人曰：“呂伯可獨立無黨者。

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Chief Councillor Li Zongmian deeply doubted Kui's words; when someone came from eastern Huai he said all censorial officials had exchanged letters with Kui—only Censor Lu did not; Zongmian then regarded Wu as worthy and said to people: "Lu Boke stands alone without faction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, left chief councillor Li Zongmian deeply doubted Kui's words; when someone came from eastern Huai he said all censorial officials had exchanged letters with Kui—only Censor Lu did not; Zongmian then regarded Wu as worthy and said to people: "Lu Boke stands alone without faction.

sentences.zh: ”嵩之得彌遠人才簿，心知敬午而內怨所論邊事。

translations.literal: " Songzhi obtained Miyuan's talent register and inwardly respected Wu yet inwardly resented his discussion of frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Songzhi obtained Miyuan's talent register; he respected Wu in his heart yet inwardly resented his discussion of frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 及午移浙東提刑，嵩之令鄧詠嗾重復亨論罷，中外不直嵩之。

translations.literal: When Wu was transferred to eastern Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner, Songzhi had Deng Yong incite Zhong Fufu to memorialize for dismissal; within and without none thought Songzhi was in the right.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu was transferred to eastern Zhejiang surveillance commissioner, Songzhi had Deng Yong incite Zhong Fufu to memorialize for dismissal; within and without none thought Songzhi was in the right.

sentences.zh: 提舉崇禧觀，再移浙東提刑。

translations.literal: He was put in charge of Chongxi Abbey, then again transferred to eastern Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of Chongxi Abbey, then again transferred to eastern Zhejiang surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 復為監察御史，入見，帝曰：“卿向來議論甚明切。

translations.literal: Again appointed Investigating Censor, he entered for audience; the emperor said: "Your previous discussions were very clear and incisive.
translations.idiomatic: Again appointed investigating censor, he entered for audience; the emperor said: "Your previous discussions were very clear and incisive.

sentences.zh: ”兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: " He concurrently served as Lecturer of the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He concurrently served as lecturer of the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 嵩之雅不欲午在經筵，時殿中侍御史項容孫子娶午從子，嵩之俾容孫上疏避午，欲撼之去，而於法無避。

translations.literal: Songzhi had never wished Wu to be in the lecture circuit; at the time Palace Attendant Censor Xiang Rongsun's son married Wu's nephew; Songzhi had Rongsun submit a memorial to avoid Wu, wishing to drive him away, yet by law there was no avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi had never wished Wu to be in the lecture circuit; at the time palace attendant censor Xiang Rongsun's son married Wu's nephew; Songzhi had Rongsun submit a memorial to avoid Wu, wishing to drive him away, yet by law there was no avoidance.

sentences.zh: 嵩之乃與言路密謀，以為午嚐劾王瓚姻家史洽，遂以瓚為右正言，午即治裝去。

translations.literal: Songzhi then secretly plotted with the remonstrance channel, using the fact that Wu had once impeached Wang Zan's in-law Shi Qia; he then made Zan Right Direct Remonstrator, and Wu immediately packed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi then secretly plotted with the remonstrance channel, using the fact that Wu had once impeached Wang Zan's in-law Shi Qia; he then made Zan right direct remonstrator, and Wu immediately packed to leave.

sentences.zh: 上手詔趣留之，午力辭，不允，由是再留，而議論愈不合。

translations.literal: The emperor personally issued an edict urging him to stay; Wu forcefully declined; it was not permitted; from this he stayed again, yet counsel grew all the more discordant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally issued an edict urging him to stay; Wu forcefully declined; permission was refused; he stayed again, yet counsel grew all the more discordant.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎兼史院官，官至中奉大夫，間居一紀卒，年七十有七，累贈至華文閣學士、通奉大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Attendant and History Office official; his highest office reached Grand Master for Proper Service; he lived in retirement for twelve years and died at seventy-seven; he was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed up to Academician of the Huawen Pavilion and Grand Master for Communication and Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to drafting attendant and history office official; his highest office reached grand master for proper service; he lived in retirement for twelve years and died at seventy-seven; he was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed up to academician of the Huawen Pavilion and grand master for communication and service.

sentences.zh: 子沆。

translations.literal: His son was Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hong.

sentences.zh: 沆字叔朝，以恩補將仕郎。

translations.literal: Hong, styled Shuchao, entered office by grace as Gentleman for Initial Appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, whose courtesy name was Shuchao, entered office by grace as gentleman for initial appointment.

sentences.zh: 端平三年，銓試第一，授黃岩縣主簿，監西京中嶽廟者二，總領湖廣、江西、京西財賦所準備差遣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duanping he took first place in the selection examination, was appointed chief clerk of Huangyan County, twice served as supervisor of the Western Capital Central Peak Temple, and was a prepared dispatch officer of the General Office for Finance of Huguang, Jiangxi, and Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duanping he took first place in the selection examination, was appointed chief clerk of Huangyan County, twice served as supervisor of the Western Capital Central Peak Temple, and was a prepared dispatch officer of the general office for finance of Huguang, Jiangxi, and Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 改知於潛縣，重囚逸，聞沆至，自歸。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Yuqian County; a major prisoner escaped, but upon hearing Hong had arrived he returned of himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to magistrate of Yuqian County; a major prisoner escaped, but upon hearing Hong had arrived he returned of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 淮西總領辟充主管文字。

translations.literal: The western Huai General Office invited him as chief clerk for documents.
translations.idiomatic: The western Huai general office invited him as chief clerk for documents.

sentences.zh: 通判婺州，朱君章訟爭田四十有二年，吳王府爭墓二十有九年，沆皆決之。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Wuzhou, Zhu Junzhang's litigation over fields lasted forty-two years and the Wu princely establishment's litigation over a tomb twenty-nine years—Hong decided them all.
translations.idiomatic: As vice prefect of Wuzhou, Zhu Junzhang's litigation over fields had lasted forty-two years and the Wu princely establishment's litigation over a tomb twenty-nine years—Hong decided them all.

sentences.zh: 特差充提領兩浙轉運鹽事使司主管文字，又差充行在點檢贍軍激賞酒庫，曆四轄、六院之文思官告，書擬尚左右郎官事。

translations.literal: He was specially assigned chief clerk of the Office for Overseeing Two-Zhejiang Transport Salt Affairs, then assigned chief clerk of the Capital Inspection Office for Provisioning the Army and Reward Wine Stores, passing through the posts of the Four Commissions and Six Bureaus as document-drafting official of the Secretariat and drafting the affairs of left and right department officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially assigned chief clerk of the office for overseeing two-Zhejiang transport salt affairs, then assigned chief clerk of the capital inspection office for provisioning the army and reward wine stores, passing through the posts of the four commissions and six bureaus as document-drafting official of the Secretariat and drafting the affairs of left and right department officials.

sentences.zh: 賈似道議行公田，彗星見，沆請罷公田還民。

translations.literal: When Jia Sidao proposed implementing public fields, a comet appeared; Hong requested abolishing public fields and returning them to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Sidao proposed implementing public fields, a comet appeared; Hong asked that public fields be abolished and returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 及理宗崩，似道矯詔廢十七界會子，行關子，沆力言非便。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong died, Sidao forged an edict abolishing the seventeenth series of treasury notes and issuing guanzi; Hong forcefully said this was not expedient.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong died, Sidao forged an edict abolishing the seventeenth series of treasury notes and issuing guanzi; Hong forcefully argued this was not expedient.

sentences.zh: 似道大怒，調將作監簿，急令言者論寢。

translations.literal: Sidao was greatly angered and transferred him to secretary of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, urgently ordering remonstrators to memorialize for dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao was greatly angered, transferred him to secretary of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and urgently ordered remonstrators to memorialize for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 久之，與雲台觀，起知興國軍，未赴，論仍雲台觀。

translations.literal: After a long time he was granted Yuntai Abbey; he was summoned to be prefect of Xingguo Army, did not go, and was again granted Yuntai Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was granted Yuntai Abbey; he was summoned to be prefect of Xingguo Army, did not go, and was again granted Yuntai Abbey.

sentences.zh: 起知全州，未赴，與仙都觀。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be prefect of Quanzhou, did not go, and was granted Xiandu Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as prefect of Quanzhou, declined to go, and was granted Xiandu Abbey instead.

sentences.zh: 德佑元年，三學伏闕上書訟沆屈，召赴行在，沆不復出，卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou, the Three Academies knelt at the palace gate to memorialize that Hong had been wronged; he was summoned to the traveling capital; Hong did not come out again; he died at eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Deyou the Three Academies knelt at the palace gate to memorialize that Hong had been wronged; he was summoned to the traveling capital; Hong did not come out again; he died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 論曰：杜範在下僚，已有公輔之望，及入相未久而沒。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Du Fan, while still in lower office, already had the reputation of a chief minister; once he entered the chancellorship he died before long.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Du Fan, while still in lower office, already bore the reputation of a chief minister; once he entered the chancellorship he died before long.

sentences.zh: 楊簡之學，非世儒所能及，施諸有政，使人百世而不能忘，然雖享高年，不究於用，豈不重可惜也哉。

translations.literal: Yang Jian's learning was beyond what worldly Confucians could reach; applied in government it made people unable to forget him for a hundred generations—yet though he enjoyed a long life he was not fully employed; is this not greatly to be regretted?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian's learning was beyond what worldly Confucians could reach; applied in government it made him unforgettable for a hundred generations—yet though he lived to great age he was never fully employed; is this not greatly to be regretted?

sentences.zh: 張虙子諒易直，呂午風采凜然，皆有裨於世道者矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu was candid and straightforward by nature; Lu Wu's bearing was stern and awe-inspiring—both were men who benefited the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu was candid and straightforward by nature; Lu Wu's bearing was stern and awe-inspiring—both men benefited their age.
